Kuiji further constructs a rebuttal by anticipating objections from the Hīnayāna perspective, thereby demonstrating that only the simultaneous emergence of multiple consciousnesses can account for the four differentiated cognitive functions.Furthermore, Kuiji demonstrates that his rebuttal arguments ultimately converge on his own Vijñaptimātratā inference, which establishes the doctrine of “everything is consciousness”.According to the theory of the eight consciousnesses, the ālaya-vijñāna, relying on karmic seeds, manifests and cognizes the external natural world and one’s physical body. The manas-vijñāna, depending on the subjective aspect (darśanabhāga) of the ālaya-vijñāna, manifests and cognizes the image of the self. The six consciousnesses, relying on the objective aspect (nimitta-bhāga) of the ālaya-vijñāna, manifest and cognize their respective objects.In this framework, all phenomena (dharmas) are inseparable from consciousness. The necessity of positing both ālaya-vijñāna and manas-vijñāna to account for the discrimination of the external world, the body, and the self is substantiated by Kuiji’s rebuttal arguments. However, the Hīnayāna tradition, while acknowledging that the six consciousnesses discriminate objects such as material dharmas, does not accept that these objects are inseparable from consciousness.To address this, Kuiji cites Xuanzang’s Vijñaptimātratā inference as a logical proof to establish the inseparability of object and consciousness.
keywords_en: Condensed Commentary on the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra (瑜伽師地論略纂)
Vijñaptimātratā in terms of principle (理唯識)

articles.title_kr: 『중론송』의 공성에 관한 고찰 - ｢관사제품｣ 제7송을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Consideration of śūnyatā in Mūlamadhyamakakārikā - Focusing on the 7th verse of the 24th chapter -
articles.abstract_kr: This thesis examines emptiness (śūnyatā) in the Mūlamadhya makakārikā (MMK). Specifically, it refers not only to Candrakīr ti’s commentary Prasannapadā (PP) but also to other verses of the 24th chapter and to various chapters of the MMK, in order to clarify “the purpose of emptiness (śūnyatā prayojana)”, “empti ness (śūnyatā)”, and “the meaning of emptiness (śūnyatārtha)” m entioned in the 7th verse of that chapter.Emptiness, as can be seen from MMK 24:1-7 and MMK 13:1-4, is neither being (bhāva), which possesses the inherent nature of existence, nor non-being (abhāva), which possesses the inherent nature of non-existence; it is the non-inherent nature (niḥsvabhāvatv a), the characteristic that makes transformation possible.The meaning of emptiness, as can be seen from MMK 24:18, becomes clearly manifest within the equivalence relation “depen dent co-arising (pratītyasamutpāda) = emptiness = temporary designation (prajñapti) = the middle way (madhyamā pratipa d),” which is established on the basis of “non-inherent nature,” that is, “not arising while possessing inherent nature.” At this point, the meaning of emptiness is identical with the meaning of dependent co-arising (the mutual dependence of causes and conditions and the arising of things as their result), temporary designation (the designation of emptiness that depends on its o wn constituents), and the middle way (emptiness in which there is neither the inherent nature of existence nor the inherent nat ure of non-existence).Finally, the purpose of emptiness, as can be seen from MMK 18:1-5, can be understood in relation to the twelve links (dvādaśāṅga pratītyasamutpāda). In connection with both the structure of the state conditioned by deluded mind (pravṛtti mārga) and the state conditioned by true mind (nivṛtti mārga) of the twelve links, the purpose of emptines is the “cessation of conceptual proliferations (prapañca),” the “extinction of discriminations (vikalpa),” the “ext inction of karma (karman) and afflictions (kleśa),” and “liberation (mokṣa),” namely the “accomplishment of the state conditioned by true mind of the twelve links.” As discussed above, when the purpose of emptiness, emptiness, and the meaning of emptiness are interpreted not only in connec tion with the commentary but also organically with various chap ters of the MMK, their significance becomes all the more clear.
articles.abstract_en: 본 논문은 『중론송』의 공성에 관해 고찰한다. 구체적으로 말하자면, ｢관사제품｣ 제7송에 언급된 ‘공성의 목적’, ‘공성’, ‘공성의 의미’를 자세히 밝히기 위해 월칭의 주석서인 󰡔쁘라산나빠다󰡕는 물론이고, ｢관사제품｣의 다른게송들과 󰡔중론송󰡕의 여러 품까지도 참고한다.공성은 ｢관사제품｣ 제1-7송과 ｢관행품｣ 제1-4송을 통해 알 수 있듯이, 존재성이라는 자성을 지닌 존재도 아니고 비존재성이라는 자성을 지닌 비존재도 아닌 것이며, 변화를 가능하게 하는 특성인 무자성이다.공성의 의미는 ｢관사제품｣ 제18송을 통해 알 수 있듯이, ‘무자성’, 즉 ‘자성을 지닌 채로 발생하지 않는 것’을 매개로 하여 성립하는 ‘연기 = 공성= 가시설 = 중도’의 등가적 관계 가운데 분명히 드러난다. 이때 공성의의미는 연기(인과 연의 상호의존성과 그 과로서 사물이 발생하는 것), 가시설(공성의 가시설이 자신의 부분을 의존하는 것), 중도(공성 가운데 존재성이라는 자성도 없고 비존재성이라는 자성도 없는 것)의 의미와 같다.마지막으로 공성의 목적은 ｢관법품｣ 제1-5송 통해 알 수 있듯이, 십이연기와 관련하여 이해할 수 있다. 십이연기의 유전문과 환멸문과 관련하여알 수 있는 공성의 목적은 ‘희론의 멸진’, ‘분별의 소멸’, ‘업과 번뇌의 소멸’, ‘해탈’, 즉 ‘환멸문의 성취’이다.이상과 같이 공성의 목적, 공성, 공성의 의미는 주석서뿐만 아니라,『중론송』의 여러 품과 유기적으로 연결하여 해석할 때, 그 뜻이 더욱더 분명히 드러난다

articles.title_kr: 불교와 유목민 문화에 관한 고찰 –대비심의 관점에서-
articles.title_en: Buddhism and Nomadic Culture: In the Perspective of Compassion (snying rje)
articles.abstract_kr: 유목민족(遊牧民族)은 동북아시아와 중앙아시아 역사를 통틀어 대승불교의 발전과 확산 과정에 많은 영향을 주었다. 고대 서북인도부터 중세 아시아 각지에 이르기까지, 유목민족은 재가신자와 승려, 후원자 등의 역할을 적극적으로 수행했을 뿐 아니라 불법의 전파에도 직간접적으로 관여되어 왔다. 중관으로 대표되는 대승(보살승)과 밀승(금강승)의 두 측면을 모두 가진 티베트 불교는 유목민족과 불교의 관계를 잘 드러내는 대표적 사례이다. 본 연구에서는 유목민족들의 사고관이 대승불교, 나아가 티베트불교와 가지는 접점에 주목하여, 각각 환경적 측면과 사회적 측면, 그리고문화적 측면에서 분석해본다. 그리고 이를 바탕으로 일부 유목민족들이 불교를 적극적으로 수용한 직간접적 사유와, 그들이 불교에 어떤 영향을 끼쳤을지에 대해 고찰해본다. 지리적으로, 유목민족들은 일찍이 원거리 무역이 발달했는데, 이는 외부 신앙과 사상 유입을 용이하게 한다. 사회적으로는 행정인력과 식자층의 수요를 승려들이 해소하면서 지도층과의 상호의존관계가 형성되었다. 문화적으로는 사냥, 도축, 전쟁 등 죽음이 일상적인 반면, 가축을 정성껏 돌보고 가족애를 중시하는 대조적 측면이 함께 존재한다. 이는 죽음 너머의 가치, 그리고 자비와 중생의 구제를 설하는 대승불교및 금강승 불교 수용에 영향을 주었을 수 있으며, 나아가 티베트 불교에서자비심의 강조와 폭력적 이미지의 등장이 함께 나타나는 배경일 수 있다.유목민적 불교의 현존 사례인 티베트 불교에서 드러나는 방편 및 지혜의불이(不二)적 시각과 대비심(大悲心)의 강조는 북인도 밀교의 기반에 유목민적 사유관이 습합되어 발전한 영향일 수 있다.
articles.abstract_en: Nomadic peoples played a pivotal role in the development and dissemination of Mahāyāna Buddhism across Northeast and Central Asia. From Northwestern India to North and East Asia, nomads have actively served various roles as lay followers, monks, and patrons, partaking in the transmission of Buddhist teachings. Tibetan Buddhism, which encompasses both Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna traditions, represents the link between nomadic societies and Buddhism. This study focuses on the intersections of nomadic thought in relation to Mahāyāna and Tibetan Vajrayāna, studying it in environmental, social, and cultural perspectives, discussing the backdrops affecting the nomadic acceptance of Buddhism, and the potential nomadic influence on Buddhism. Geographically, long-distance trade routes of Nomads have facilitated the introduction of foreign religions and ideas. Socially, Buddhist monks undertook the role of administrative manpower, fostering reciprocal relationships with nomadic rulers. Culturally, the coexistence of contrasting ideas, such as common death in hunting, slaughter, and warfare, and care for livestock and familial bonds may have have become a factor in the reception of Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna; possibly pursuit of values beyond death, of compassion, and salvation of sentient beings, potentially contributing to the concurrent display of compassionate ideals and violent imagery in Tibetan Buddhism. The emphasis on non-dual perspective and the use of skillful means, and great compassion (snying rje chen po) prevalent in Tibetan Buddhism may thus be the influence of nomadic thoughts amalgamated with, and on the foundations of, North Indian Tantric Buddhism.

articles.title_kr: 『수현기』 법계연기설의 지(智)에 대한 분석
articles.title_en: Jñāna of the Dharma-dhātu Dependent Origination  theory in Zhiyan’s Souxuanji
articles.abstract_kr: This paper aims to analyze Zhiyan’s Dharma-dhātu Dependent Origination theory presented in the Souxuanji, which is widely regarded as a representative model of Huayan's dependent origination from Dharma-dhātu. To explain the practical aspects of Zhiyan’s Dharma-dhātu Dependent Origination theory, an understanding of jñāna is indispensable.In light of the above scholarly concerns, this study reviews the interpretations of jñāna found in previous research, clarifies the divergence of opinion among them, and emphasizes the need to clearly define the various concepts of jñāna as a key issue to address.To tackle this task, the study adopts the framework of the three types of Nirvikalpa-jñāna found in the Mahāyānasaṃgraha to elucidate the role and significance of jñāna in Zhiyan’s Dharma-dhātu Dependent Origination theory. The study concludes that, in Zhiyan’s theory, jñāna constitutes the core concept in the attainment of samyag-jñāna (正體智) through the cultivation of prayoga-jñāna (加行智). This highlights the practical significance of jñāna in emboding Dharma-dhātu Dependent Origination.In other words, the purpose of explaining this theory is to enable practitioners to awaken to it, with the practice of prayoga-jñāna and the attainment of fundamental Nirvikalpa-jñāna being essential stages in the cultivation process.

articles.title_kr: 『수현기』에 나타난 불퇴설(不退說)의 교판적 의미
articles.title_en: Doctrinal Taxonomy and the Theory of  Non-retrogression in the Suixuanji[搜玄記]
articles.abstract_kr: This study aims to examine the theory of non-retrogression[不 退] as presented in Zhiyan’s[智儼] commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Dafangguang fo Huayanjing souxuan fenqi tongzhi fanggui[大方廣佛華嚴經搜玄分齊通智方軌] from a doctrinal taxonomy[敎判]. Its purpose is to clarify the ideological significance of non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles[三乘] and the One Vehicle[一乘] in Huayan doctrine. In Mahayana Buddhism, ‘retrogression (退)’ and ‘non-retrogression (不退)’ are core tasks directly linked to the theory of Buddhahood[成佛論], transcending the simple success or failure of practice.Particularly in Huayan doctrine, non-retrogression holds a dual meaning as both a gateway for entering enlightenment and the ultimate achievement.First this paper analyzes the aspects of retrogression described from the standpoint of the Three Vehicles, focusing on the theories of the Four, Two, and Three Types of Retrogression. Through this, it demonstrates how Zhiyan critically adopted and inherited the theories of the Dilun[地論], Shelun[攝論], and Sanlun[三論] schools while establishing origi-68 / 보조사상 74집(2026. 03) nal concepts such as ‘retrogression even in the absence of progress’[不進退亦退].Notably, it argues that non-retrogression in the Three Vehicles is merely a provisional teaching partially realized only upon reaching the Ten Grounds[十地].In the subsequent investigation of the One Vehicle’s theory of non-retrogression, this study elucidates the unique Huayan logic focusing on the stages of Faith[信位] and Understanding[解 位]. Zhiyan asserts that entry into the One Vehicle occurs through "indestructible faith" at the completion of the Ten Faiths. Furthermore, by showing the first stage of the Ten Abodes[十住] constitutes non-retrogression, he solidifies the doctrinal basis for the Huayan principle that "at the very moment of the first aspiration, one achieves correct enlightenment"[初發心時便成正覺].Finally, through the theory of "Non-existence of Retrogression"[無退說], which posits that the original nature of Samantabhadra is inherently free from retrogression, he reveals the essence of Huayan’s "manifestation of nature"[性 起] thought.In conclusion, Zhiyan’s theory of non-retrogression does not merely explain the stages of practice; it serves as a key mechanism for clarifying the doctrinal transition from the Three Vehicles to the One Vehicle and for asserting the distinctiveness of Huayan.

articles.title_kr: 지엄(智儼)의 불타관(佛陀觀)
articles.title_en: Zhiyan(智儼)’s Perspective on the Buddha
articles.abstract_kr: According to the Souxuanji(『搜玄記』), Zhiyan defines the Buddha as one who is both self-awakened and capable of awakening others. The manifestation of the Buddha-body and the principle of dependent origination presented in the Souxuan ji together form the doctrinal foundation of Zhiyan’s Perspective on the Buddha.The Huayanwushiyaowenda(『華嚴五十要問答』) explains that practitioners initially arouse faith through seeing and hearing the Ten Buddhas (十佛) of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, and that without the power of the Buddha’s sāgara-mudrā-samādhi(海印三 昧), seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma would not be possible. Although Buddhahood is realized simultaneously by the Buddha and sentient beings in each moment, The attainment of higher stages through Buddhist practice is based on the principle of dependent origination.

articles.title_kr: 『법집별행록절요병입사기』의 구성과 선오후수 수행의 전개
articles.title_en: The Structure of  Beopjipbyeolhaengnok Jeoryo Byeongip Sagi and the Unfolding of Enlightenment-Driven Practice (先悟後修) as a Practice System
articles.abstract_kr: This study examines the structure of Byeolhaengnok Jeoryo Byeongip Sagi (法集別行錄節要幷入私記), a late work of Jinul, and argues that its organization reflects a progressive deepening of the practice system known as enlightenment-driven practice, which embodies the organic relationship between sudden enlightenment and gradual cultivation. Rather than treating the text as a mere compilation of disparate practices, this study interprets it as a systematically organized guide to contemplative practice.The text consists of three parts: Jeoryo (Excerpts), Sagi (Personal Commentary), and Jinul’s own exposition of practice. The Jeoryo section establishes an ideal model based on the Heze school’s notion of the mind as serene and luminous awareness (空寂靈知), defining a path that proceeds from sudden enlightenment through gradual cultivation to final realization.The Sagi section deepens this framework by correcting misconceptions concerning samādhi and prajñā, introducing the path of non-abiding (無心合道), and subsuming various doctrinal models of practice under the framework of this practice system.Jinul’s own practice theory further advocates the Chan method of complete rejection (全揀門) as the means of sudden enlightenment and emphasizes that authentic cultivation must be grounded in realization. Notably, rather than merely presenting the teaching of Wondon Ohae (圓頓悟解) as a systematic doctrinal framework, Jinul further articulates the Gyeongjeol-mun (徑截門) as a practical leap that cuts off conceptual elaboration and leads to the ultimate state.In conclusion, Byeolhaengnok Jeoryo Byeongip Sagi unfolds as a structured progression: presenting an ideal model, providing theoretical clarification, and reaching a practical culmination. This structural analysis demonstrates that the text functions as a coherent and comprehensive manual for this practice system.
keywords_en: Byeolhaengnok Jeoryo Byeongip Sagi(法集別行錄節要幷入私記)

articles.title_kr: 태고보우의 선시로 보는 세간과 출세간 - 『太古和尙語錄』을 중심으로
articles.title_en: The Mundane and Supramundane seen through Seon  Poems of Taego Bou (太古普愚) in Recorded Quotes of  Seon Master Taego (太古和尙語錄)
articles.abstract_kr: Taego Bou (太古普愚, 1301–1382) is often portrayed as embodying a dual identity as both a politically engaged cleric and a devoted practitioner, shaped by his ties to the Yuan and Goryeo royal courts. This has led to his actions being interpreted as an example of the “Perfect Integration of the Two Truths,” uniting the mundane and the supramundane. However, upon tracing his life chronologically, a different picture emerges. Through the mechanism by which inner emotions surface in his poetry, the dissonance between his spiritual practice and worldly engagement becomes openly visible. Beneath the ideal of integration lie unresolved tensions and inner suffering.Previous studies on Taego’s thought and historical role were focused on his literary works, especially his poetry, have been often limited to partial quotations or appreciation. Yet the essence of practice revealed in his Poems of Awakening, including the process of realization and its confirmation, cannot be adequately understood through fragmentary literary analysis alone. Particularly, the conflict between his controversial politi-cal involvement and his spiritual path can only be grasped by examining his life and poems together. As poetry serves to verbalize the unconscious, Taego’s Zen poems disclose his true intent. Tracing his life through poetry thus offers insight into how unavoidable conflicts of the mundane may become either an obstacle to practice or its very driving  force.
keywords_en: Entering the Bonds and  Extending a Hand (入廛垂手)

articles.title_kr: 조선 후기 능엄사기(楞嚴私記)에 나타난 연담(蓮潭)과 인악(仁岳)의 주석 경향과 강학(講學) 교류에 대한 소고 - 『능엄경요해』권1의 해제(解題)를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Study of the Commentarial Tendencies and Scholarly (講學) Exchange between Yeondam and Inak in Late-Joseon Śūraṅgama Sūtra Sagi (楞嚴私記): Focusing on the Explanatory Introduction of Volume 1 of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra Yohae
articles.abstract_kr: This paper, among the private notes (私記) for each subject in the 講院 curriculum written by Yeondam and Inak in the late Joseon Dynasty, the two Gangbaek's commentarial tendencies and traces of scholarly (講學) exchange, focusing on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra Sagi. Until now, the exchange of scholarly between the two Gangbaek has been drawn negatively at first glance, but there has been a discussion recently that Inak has reviewed the traces of referring to Yeondam's views. This paper is a comparative review of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra Sagi of the two Gangbaek based on the lifting of Volume 1 of Śūraṅgama Sūtra Yohae on the same line.First, in Chapter II, the annotation trends of Yeondam and Inak were compared and analyzed. As a result, the annotation trends of Yeondam and Inak in Śūraṅgama Sūtra Sagi could be defined as 'Tongseok(通釋)' and 'Byeolseok(別釋)', respectively, and the examples were also shown. It is believed that the two Gangbaek's Śūraṅgama Sūtra Sagi acted as a macroscopic framework and a microscopic framework for the younger student who learned Śūraṅgama Sūtra, respectively. However, this can be understood as a seemingly contradictory annotation trend, but rather, it is also the point that reveals a mature aspect that coexisted as the tradition of the late Joseon Dynasty's Śūraṅgama Sūtra annotation complements each other.In Chapter III, the background of the times and related records are summarized together as a basis for reconsidering the existing perceptions after examining the traces of scholarly exchange. As a result, it was confirmed how Inak presented conceptual explanations such as on Yeondam's Śūraṅgama Sūtra Sagi, Doseo Sagi, and Jeolyo in his own way. This is considered to be a trace of Inak's unraveling of the teaching traditions of Korean Buddhism, including the views of Yeondam. On the other hand, until now, the relationship between the two Gangbaek's scholarly exchange has been understood negatively. This is considered to be a remnant of the pain of the times when the national authority was robbed and the Joseon Dynasty was distort by the colonial view. And its impact is currently ongoing.In the future, we hope that the endless review and research related to the morale of the two Gangbaek will reveal the true nature of the two Gangbaek's commentarial tendencies and scholarly exchanges, and that the fog that is thick in Buddhism in the late Joseon Dynasty will clear up.
keywords_en: scholarly exchange of late Joseon period

articles.title_kr: 『삼문직지(三門直指)』 염불문의 ‘염불’ 개념 - 염불의 종류를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: On the Concept of‘Yeombul(Buddhānusmṛti)’ in Sammunjikji - focused on the category of‘Yeombul’-
articles.abstract_kr: This article aims to consider the concept of ‘Yeombul(念佛)’ in Sammunjikji(Instructions on three Entrances in Buddhism, 三門 直指), in which the compiler Jinheo Palgwan(振虛捌關) collected many kinds of Yeombul in the history of Buddhism. He divided it into two kinds of Yeombul, I.e recollection in everyday life and recollection in deathbed. In detail, He also divided recollection in everyday life into ten kinds of recollection, two kinds of recollection, four kinds of recollection, five kinds of recollection, and recollection as superior behaviour.When I examined his classification, I found out there are some mistakes and misunderstandings in his description.Firstly, he divided two kinds of recollection into oral recollection(口念) and mindful recollection(心念). Moreover, he divided mindful recollection into observation in meditation(觀想念 佛) and whole observation(雜觀). But his classification is very easy to misunderstand. I think that it is correct to understand oral recollection as oral recitation of Amitabha’s Name and mindful recollection as observation in meditation. If I suppose ‘(pure observation, 純觀)’ which can embrace observation on Pure Land(淨觀) and observation oneself in Pure Land(坐觀), mindful recollection(=observation in meditation) could be divided into ‘(pure observation)’ and whole observation. And it is well-organized classification we can understand in ease.Secondly, there are some mistakes in which Jinheo Palgwan cited classifications from the history of Buddhism. When he recalled five kinds of recollection from Vasubandh’s concept of five observations(五念門), he took a mistake to invert order of vow-making and observation. Because vow-making is related with śamatha(止) and observation is related with vipaśyāna(觀), it is correct to refer vow-making before mentioning observation.Thirdly, It is incorrect Jinheo Palgwan’s citation to count the eight behaviours(aṣṭadharma) in Vimalakīrtinirdeṣa as superior Yeombul(勝行念佛). It will hinder every person not to concentrate his recollection on Pure Land or recitation Amitabha’s Name.In brief, we can understand that the concept of ‘Yeombul’ in Sammunjikji is not only the recitation of Amitabha’s Name but also the co-exisitence between precept(śīla) and Seon, between recitation of Amitabha’s Name and observation in meditation, recitation of Amitabha’s Name and bodhisattva’s practice.

articles.title_kr: 조주선(趙州禪)의 ‘방하착(放下著)’ 원리를 활용한 현대적 명상 프로그램 설계 연구: - 마음챙김(MBSR)의 기능주의적 한계에 대한 존재론적 대안을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Study on the Design of a Modern Meditation  Program Utilizing the Principle of ‘Bang-ha-chak’  (Letting Go) in Zhaozhou Seon: Focusing on an  Ontological Alternative to the Functionalist Limitations  of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR)
articles.abstract_kr: The purpose of this study is to re-examine the core tenets of Zhaozhou Seon (趙州禪) and propose an ontological alternative to the functionalist limitations of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) through the principle of ‘Letting Go’ (Banghachak, 放下著). Zhaozhou Seon deconstructs language and concepts through Seon dialogues (Gong-an) such as ‘Mu’ (無), ‘Ordinary Mind is the Way’ (平常心是道), and ‘Go Drink Tea’ (喫茶去), emphasizing the awakening of one's Original Face (本 來面目) in daily life. This study re-establishes the ideology of Zhaozhou Seon into a tripartite structure: ‘Letting Go (Banghachak) - Everyday Life (Ordinary Mind) - No-Mind (Mushin).’ Specifically, by presenting the conceptual foundation of Sunyata (空性, Emptiness) inherent in ‘Mushin’ as a prerequisite for practice, this study proposes an eight-week meditation program designed to prevent practitioners from falling into spiritual bypasses such as Mugigong (無記空, blank emptiness) and to induce an ontological shift through Seongseong-jeok-jeok (惺惺寂寂, vivid awakening and serene stillness).The step-by-step composition of the program is as follows: First, in the ‘Banghachak’ stage, it moves beyond the non-judgmental attention of MBSR to promote a return to the original self through an ‘extraordinary expedient’ (格外之方便) that immediately cuts off all discriminative delusions. Second, in the ‘Everyday Life’ stage, it aims for the integration of practice and life (Cham-haeng, 參行) based on Zhaozhou’s philosophy of Ordinary Mind. Third, in the ‘Mushin’ stage, it realizes fundamental freedom by integrating previous practices and experiencing the functioning of Mu-yong-gong (無用功, effortless action) where the distinction between subject and object is extinguished. This experience is then extended to the daily practice of Borim (保任) and Ip-jeon-su-su (入纏垂手) as a form of Hoihyang (回向, merit-transference). This study holds academic significance by reinterpreting traditional Seon Buddhist thought within a modern practical context, adding ontological depth to the discourse of meditation beyond mere psychological healing. However, as this program is a proposal at the theoretical design stage, empirical verification through a pilot test is required in the future.

articles.title_kr: 사띠 및 마음챙김의 轉用에 관한 비교 연구 - 고엔카의 위빳사나와 존 카밧진의 MBSR을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Comparative Study on the Sati and the Appropriation of Mindfulness - Focusing on S.N. Goenka’s Vipassana and  Jon Kabat-Zinn’s MBSR -
articles.abstract_kr: This study addresses the issues and alternatives arising from the adaptation of sati from practice to modern mindfulness. Jon Kabat-Zinn’s Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) has garnered significant attention from both the field of psychology and the general public by reconstructing the Vipassanā practice of Southern Buddhism. However, MBSR has faced criticism for lacking historical and philological grounding in its Buddhist origins and for degenerating into "McMindfulness"—a commodified product that merely packages the essence of practice. To elucidate the factors contributing to this phenomenon, this study compares S. N. Goenka’s Vipassanā—which indirectly influenced Kabat-Zinn—with Kabat-Zinn’s MBSR. A quantitative analysis of the foundational texts of both systems reveals that, despite employing similar terminology, they differ fundamentally in their conceptual usage, purpose of practice, and ethical foundations. This study aims to minimize contextual distortion in the transition of practice and help modern meditation programs establish a more complete structure. To this end, it proposes two alternatives necessary for continuity when transitioning from sati practice to therapeutic mindfulness: first, the internalization of ethics based on the interdependent (mutually reliant) composition of the Threefold Training; and second, an approach that preserves the essence of practice rooted in the principles of the Threefold Training while reconstructing it complementarily with modern therapeutic goals.

articles.title_kr: 아지비카 니야티(niyati) 개념의 두 해석과 그 실천적 함의
articles.title_en: Two Interpretations of the Ājīvika Concept of Niyati and Its Practical Implications
articles.abstract_kr: Jainism as a major śramaṇa movement in ancient India, presents unique methodological challenges: no primary texts survive, and our knowledge depends entirely on descriptions in Buddhist and Jain polemical literature. This paper examines interpretations of the Ājīvika concept of niyati (fate, necessity, determinism) by constructing two ideal types—rigid determinism and compromised determinism—and comparing their theoretical implications for the relationship between niyati, karma, religious practice, and liberation.Drawing on the methodological caution advocated by scholars such as Bronkhorst regarding traditions known only through other-tradition sources, this study analyzes key passages from the Sāmañ aphala Sutta, Sūyagaḍāṅga, and Uvāsagadasāo to address three questions: (1) Does niyati replace karma or encompass it as a higher-order principle? (2) Is ascetic practice a cause producing effects or a predetermined part of the cosmic process? (3) What role could deterministic teachers offer to lay followers? mic principle that nullifies the moral efficacy of karma, relegating practice to a ritual marking the completion of a predetermined cycle. The compromised determinism model suggests that Ājīvikas may have denied the erasure of past karma while accepting the possibility of preventing new karma accumulation, thus preserving a limited role for ascetic discipline.This comparative analysis reveals that each interpretive model not only offers different solutions to the determinism-practice paradox but also corresponds to divergent historical trajectories: assimilation into Jainism versus transformation into theistic devotionalism. By treating these models as heuristic tools rather than historical facts, this paper argues that doctrines appearing self-contradictory at the theoretical level can achieve their own coherence when examined in relation to the practices they sustain—ascetic discipline, lay devotion, and communal organization.

60권 5호.abstract_kr: Yoon (2000) presents a set of mechanisms of verbal humor and proposes a theory of humor based on three global principles, namely, 'relief from seriousness,' 'omniscience,' and 'deviation from the standard.' Given this, this paper examines Korean verbal humor data to see if the mechanisms and the theory of humor presented in Yoon (2000) with English data also fit into Korean data. Some differences between English and Korean verbal humor represented in English and Korean sitcom data are also presented. It will be shown that there are some mechanisms of humor on which especially Korean humor data heavily rely which will reveal some aspects of the cultural differences between English and Korean verbal humor.

17권 호.abstract_kr: 거기에 필요에 따라 자신의 견해(私記)를 첨부한 것이지만, 지눌 사상의 전모를 가장 포괄적으로 담고 있다는 점에서 그 자신의 저술로 간주해도 무방하다. 나는 이 논문에서 『절요』가 지눌 사상 일반에서 차지하고 있는 위치를 지눌의 여타 저술들과의 관계를 살펴보면서 논하고 이를 통해서 지눌 선 사상의 전체 구도를 밝혀보고자 한다.禪의 생명은 그 생동성에 있으며 선은 본래 체계나 구조를 혐오하지만 지눌의 선사상은 비교적 체계성과 논리적 정합성이 강한 편이다. 그 이유를 정확히 밝히기는 쉽지 않지만, 아마도 그것은 지눌이 無師獨悟한 禪師였다는 사실과 무관하지 않을 것이다. 고려 중기 무신집권의 사회적 혼란기에 禪敎의 대립과 도덕적 타락으로 혼탁해진 불교계에 입문하여 일정한 스승 없이(學無常師)  구도의 길을 걷는다는 것은 대단한 주체성을 요한 일이었을 것이며, 자기가 걷고 있는 길에 대한 부단한 반성과 체계적 숙고를 요구했을 것이다. 물론 우리는 지눌의 저술들이 전부 남아 있지 않은 상황에서 이 문제에 대해서 속단을 해서는 안 된다. 지눌에게는 『修心訣』, 『眞心直說』, 『圓頓成佛論』, 『看話決疑論』과 같이 선 수행에 관한 이론적 저술만 있었던 것은 아니고 『上堂錄』, 『法語』, 『歌頌』 같은 것도 있었음을 「비명」은 전하고 있다.  이들이 우리에게 전해졌더라면 아마도 우리는 지눌 선의 다른 면을 볼 수 있었을지도 모른다. 실제로 「비명」은 지눌이 임종 전에 문인들과 나눈 문답을 소개하고 있는데 활달한 선사로서의 그의 면모를 유감 없이 보여주고 있다.  그러나 다른 한 편, 지눌이 선에 관하여 이론적 성격이 짙은 저술들을 다수 남겼다는 것은 선사로서의 그의 특성 가운데 하나라고 평할 수 있으며, 그의 저술들 속에 발견되는 사상의 명료성과 체계성은 그로 하여금 한국 불교사에 지속적 영향을 미칠 수 있게 만든 한 요인이 되었을 것이다.그의 저술들 가운데서도 『절요』는 그의 만년의 저술로서 선의 이론과 실천 양면에서 그의 사상을 가장 포괄적으로 보여주고 있다. 그러나 『절요』는 지눌 사상을 구성하고 있는 다양한 주제들을 거의 총망라하여 다루고 있기 때문에 『수실결』이나『진심직설』과 같은 다른 저술에 비해 복잡한 구조를 가지고 있으며 체계성이 다소 떨어지는 산만한 저술이라는 느낌을 주는 것도 부인하기 어려운 사실이다. 따라서 우리는 『절요』에서 지눌이 다루고 있는 다양한 주제들을 그의 다른 저술들과 대비해보면서 지눌 사상의 전체 구도와 체계를 밝힐 필요가 있다.

17권 호.title_kr: 杜順과 法界觀門에 대한 小考
17권 호.title_en: The Study of Du-shun(杜順) and The Fa-jie-guan-men(法界觀門)
17권 호.abstract_kr: If we are looking carefully at the definition of studies on Hua-yen, which is said that it is an huge system based on Huayan jing(華嚴經) of which is the basis of Hua-yen thought(華嚴思想), and also based on Ancestor of Hua-yen sect. So it is easy to understand the importance of the Ancestor of Hua-yen sect(華嚴宗)In this meaning I tried to examining the Du-shun(杜順) as a first Ancestors. But there were only few texts reminded to introduce his thought. The Fa-jie-guan-men(法界觀門), of which considered as his solitarly text. But currently some scholars are doubt on Du-shun(杜順)'s authority.Since it is so, it is difficult to clear up statue of his thought by examining some subsist texts in positively way. As the one who has many writings is not always the good thinker, there is no relationship between importanceness as a religious man of Du-shun(杜順) and the fact of non-existing writings.In this way, this treatise firstly examines the Du-shun(杜順) as a first Ancestors of Hua-yen sect(華嚴初祖), and then it examines him as a Samantabhadra actor(普賢行者), of whom practices the acts of Samantabhadra. And examining the genuineness of The Fa-jie-guan-men(法界觀門), which is written experience of his religious practice, to indicate his a point of view on dicipline.It is to say,  his a point of view on dicipline is basically practice of the Buddha's original vow So it is absolutely universally and also it is materialized as a independent world. Frankly speaking, the importanceness of Du-shun(杜順)'s  Fa-jie- guan-men(法界觀門) in teachings of Hua-yen were given an new appraisal bi the period of Cheng-guan(澄觀).
17권 호.abstract_en: 두순의 사상적 입장을 전하고 있는 문헌은 아주 적다. 현재 유일한 저작이라고 대체로 인정하고 있는 법계관문도 실은 眞撰에 대하여 異說이 분분한 실정이다.법계관문의 진찬문제에 대해서는 ‘杜順 撰’이라고 기록한 최초의 목록인 圓仁의 入唐新求聖敎目錄을 비롯하여 圓超錄과 永超錄 그리고 義天錄의 기록으로 미루어보아 9세기 초기에는 본서가 존재하였음을 알 수 있고, 게다가 일본에 전래되었다는 점으로 미루어 9세기 중엽까지는 杜順撰으로 남아있었을 것이다.설사 법계관문을 ‘杜順 撰’으로 보기 어렵다고 하더라도 이 문제가 그대로 그를 화엄종 初祖로 볼 수 없다는 것을 의미하지는 않는다. 제1차 자료인 唐高僧傳에서 두순이 定業과 神異에 뛰어날 뿐만 아니라, 敎祖的 자질을 갖추고 있음을 보증하고 있다. 무엇보다도 그의 제자에 화엄종 제2조인 智儼이 명기되어 있는 점에서 한층 더 그러하다 하겠다.그리고 두순의 행적에서 그가 제자인 樊玄智에게 권했던 普賢行은 바로 그 자신의 실천행이였다. 그러므로 당고승전의 ‘受持定業’이라는 定業의 내용도 다름 아닌 보현행이었던 것이다. 이와 같이 두순의 종교적 실천생활이 보현행이었다면 그 보현행은 무엇을 의미하는가.다시 말해 두순의 보현행이란, 근본적으로는 불타의 本願으로 일관된 실천이다. 즉 절대적으로 보편적이며 또한 어디까지나 주체적 세계로써 실현되는 것을 의미한다.그러나 두순의 법계관문이 화엄교학에서 차지하는 비중은 澄觀 때에 와서야 새로운 평가가 부여된 것으로 보아야 할 것이다.

19권 호.abstract_kr: The zen-school of Tang(唐) dynasty was the essence of China zen buddhism. But, in Song(宋) dynasty, the zen action and zen thought went off their color. So, gradually vicious practices and side effects appeared in many aspect.The Ganhwa-Seon(看話禪) was a practice of zen-buddhism Especially, Ganhwa-Seon emphasis so called Hwadu(話頭). That is, Ganhwa(看話) means have a look at the Hwadu. This Ganhwa-Seon come into being in Song-dynasty of Chinese by Daehye- Jonggo(大慧宗? : 1009-1163). Here we can ratiocinate some reasons, namely, the formations come into being of Ganhwa-Seon.Firstly, We can examined that Daehye- Jonggo have the critical attitude for the thought of Silent-Penetration(墨照) by Jinhul-Chungryo(眞歇淸了). At that times, a group of the thought of Silent-Penetration lapsed into a state of coma. In many ways, this was a target of the critical attitude by Daehye-Jonggo, so called, a fancy, a foolish imaginings, a stupefaction, a sleeping sickness, a delusion, and the borderland between sleeping and waking, etc.Secondly, the attitude of a peace-at-any-price principle about all seon-practice. The ways of prudentialism was originated from the closing years of Tang-dynasty. The secondly effect on seon-buddhism were prevalent every seon-masters at the time of the early days in Song-dynasty.In this state of affairs, Daehye-Jonggo had the critical attitude for the thought of Silent-Penetration and the ways of prudentialism So, he standed by his many opinions in his "The Discrimination between right and wrong on Secn-practice(辨邪正說). At that time, Daehye-Jonggo(大慧宗? 1089-1163) set up against that problem and that followers. As a part of that preventive measure, he preached sermons for not only Buddhist priests but also high officials that The Discrimination between right and wrong on seon-practice.Here we can abstract his taught for them in eight ways.First, discriminate the expedients.Second, Alert absence of expedients.Third, Do not ignore of enlightenments.Fourth, Do not depend on letters and notions.Fifth, Only adhere The Muja-Hwagu(無字話頭) instead of divisionism.Sixth, Do not consider at own discretion.Seventh, Seek after for seon masters.Eighth, Bear in mind the faiths.These eight ways were as it used at that times, and are as it useful for modem seon practice and buddhist priests. Here we can examined some reasons about the formation come into being of Ganhwa-Seon(看話禪).
