In addition, Gaofeng-Yuanmiao, a practitioner of the Ganhwaseon看話禪 in the Yuan元 Dynasty, did not pay attention to the removal of anguish, but doubted the Hwadu話頭. During Ganhwaseon meditation, he experienced samadhi三昧 in which the subject and object disappeared. The two thinkers' theories of practices can be seen as an application of the theory of practice of the Tathāgata-garba thought, and this can be said to be a compressive transformation of the Yogācāra practice called Gyeondo見道. Zen practitioners in East Asia claimed that even ordinary people can encounter buddha nature in their daily lives without going through a long process of practice to remove defilement in the basis of Tathāgata-garba thought.

70권 호.title_en: On the Criticism of Samjong Sŏn in Udam Honggi's Sŏnmun Jeungjeongrok
70권 호.abstract_kr: Udam Honggi(1822-1881) re-confirmed the traditional interpretation of Patriarch-Sŏn=Beyond-the-norm-Sŏn, Tatagatha- Sŏn=Logic-Sŏn through the Sŏnmun Jeungjeongrok(禪門證正錄, Records of True Enlightenment of Sŏn) based on the Sŏnmunkangyochip(禪門綱要集, Collection of Essentials of the Sŏn) and the Sŏnmunyŏmsongsŏrhwa(禪門拈頌說話, Prose and Verse Comments on the Sŏn School) in order to criticize the Three Kind of Sŏn Thought. While Baekpa divided the first phrase into Patriarch-Sŏn, the second phrase into Tathagatha-Sŏn, and the third phrase into Logic-Sŏn and assigned canonical understanding to the third phrase, Udam understood the second phrase's Tathagatha-Sŏn as a self-achieving Sŏn, which means One Vehicle Teaching such as <Avatamsaka Sutra>, <Lotus Sutra>, and <Awakening of Faith>. It is also characteristic that Udam proved Patriarch-Sŏn's superiority by citing the story of Patriarch Jingwi published in Sŏnmunpojangnok(Record of the Treasure Store of the Sŏn School). Both metaphor of Killing and Healing were Patriarch-Sŏn, which had no superiority and inferiority, and Qingyuan-line and Nanyue-line passed on killing and healing, respectively, after the sixth patriarch, and four houses of Linji, Yunmen, Guiyang, and Fayan were assigned to the Nanyue-line. This is the view that inherited Sŏn'ga kugam(禪家龜鑑, Mirror of the Sŏn School) in relation to the succession of the five house of Sŏn. The Huaŏmilsŭngkyo(華嚴一乘敎, One Vehicle Teaching of Huayan) is reaffirmed as Tathagatha-Sŏn, which historical Buddha realized himself, and the relationship between Patriarch-Sŏn and Tathagatha-Sŏn is understood as Sŏn and the doctrine which means ‘Simultaneous cultivation of Sŏn and Doctrinal studies’. This idea can be understood as the result of the revelation of the succession of Master Bojo and identity of Linji lineage, which are considered to be the characteristics of Buhyu-lineage centered on Songgwangsa Temple in the late Joseon Buddhist Society.

70권 호.title_en: The meaning and value of compilation of 『JogyesanSonggwangsago(曹溪山松廣寺寺庫)』 during the Japanese colonial period
70권 호.abstract_kr: 『JogyesanSonggwangsago(曹溪山松廣寺寺庫)』is a historical record of Songgwangsa Temple. Although 『史庫(Sago)』 was carried out within the Buddhist policy of the Japanese colonial government of Joseon, it was an opportunity to establish the identity of our Buddhist history. Although it was only the history and culture of one temple, it organized Buddhist thought, practice, and religious traditions based on history, people, and sacred cultural assets. 『史庫Sasago)』 is the largest volume of temple records compiled at the same time, and its system is also highly complete. 『史庫Sasago)』 introduced the values ​​of Korean Buddhism through the traces of National Master Bojo-Jinul(普照知訥) and the 16 State Preceptors, and Joseon's records promoted the inheritance of Bojo Jinul's practice tradition. The various documents included in 『史庫Sasago)』 are also of high value as research materials as they allow us to examine the status of Songgwangsa Temple in Goryeo and Joseon, as well as the temple economy, disputes, and changes. sacred cultural assets such as the pavilion, Buddha statues, and Buddhist paintings tell the story of the temple’s prosperity and decline.The main compilers, Geummyeong Bojeong(錦溟寶鼎, 1861~ 1930), Yongeun Wanseop(龍隱完燮, 1899~1975), Kisan Seokjin(綺山錫珍, 1892~1968), and Yulam Chanui(栗庵讚儀), are also representative figures in the history of modern and contemporary Korean Buddhism. They tried to restore the tradition of missionary studies built up by the teachers of Goryeo and Joseon, and were active in renovating the decayed temple and preserving its status as a Buddhist temple. In addition, he attempted to preserve the historical materials of Songgwangsa Temple through research and collection of materials for more than 30 years, and these records played a decisive role in compiling 『史庫(Sasago)』

70권 호.title_en: Establishment and activities of the Songgwangsa Buddhist Youth Association during the Japanese colonial period
70권 호.abstract_kr: Japan imposed cultural rule after the March 1st Movement in 1919. A cultural movement arose in Korean society to overcome the colonial system. In June 1920, the Joseon Buddhist Youth Association was established. Buddhist Youth Association branches were established throughout the country.In August 1920, the Songgwangsa Buddhist Youth Association was established. During the Japanese colonial period, Songgwangsa Temple sent many students to study in Gyeongseong and Japan. Those from Songgwangsa Temple who were studying in Seoul participated in the Joseon Buddhist Youth Association. Those who studied abroad in Japan participated in the Joseon Buddhist Youth Association in Japan.After graduating from school, they returned to Songgwangsa Temple and engaged in educational activities. They participated in the establishment of the Beolgyo Buddhist Youth Association.In March 1931, the Korean Buddhist Youth Union was established. Members of the Songgwangsa Buddhist Youth Association were active in the Gyeongseong Buddhist Youth Union, the Beolgyo Buddhist Youth Union, and the Tokyo Buddhist Youth Union in Japan.
70권 호.abstract_en: 3.1운동 이후 일제는 무단통치에서 문화통치로 전환하였다. 한국 사회에는 식민지 체제를 극복하고 자주적 역량을 높이려는 운동이 일어났다. 불교 청년들도 이런 사회적 흐름에 동참하여 1920년 6월 20일 조선불교청년회를 설립하였다. 이어 전국의 불교 청년들이 지회를 설립하며 동참하였다.송광사 불교청년회는 1920년 8월경에 설립되었다. 참여 회원이 100여 명에 이르는 규모였으나 전해지는 자료가 없어 전모를 파악하기 힘들다. 그 점을 보완하기 위해 송광사 출신으로 경성과 일본에서 불교청년회 활동을 한 인물들을 주목하였다. 타지에서 불교청년회 활동에 참여하였다면 송광사에 있을 때 불교청년회 회원이었을 가능성이 높기 때문이다.송광사 출신으로 1920년대 중앙의 조선불교청년회 활동에 참여한 인물이 많았다. 1929년 1월 실행한 조선불교선교양종대회의 사전 발기회와 당일 행사 진행에 송광사 출신들의 참여도가 높았다. 일본에 유학한 사람들은 재일본조선불교청년회의 평의원과 부서 간사를 맡아 조직을 이끌었다. 1921년 하기방학 때 조직된 순회강연단 일원으로 국내를 순회하며 계몽운동을 전개하였다. 그들은 학교를 졸업한 뒤 송광사로 돌아와 교육활동을 하였고 벌교불교청년회가 설립될 때 많은 도움을 주었다.1931년 이후 조선불교청년회는 조선불교청년총동맹으로 전환되었다. 송광사 불교청년회 출신들은 경성동맹이 출범하자 적극적으로 참여하였다. 송광사 불교청년회와 벌교불교청년회가 합쳐 벌교동맹이 되자 초기 동맹의 집행부를 맡아 활동 방향을 정립하였다. 그리고 일본에서 동경동맹이 출범하자 임원이 되어 적극적으로 동맹을 이끌었다.
keywords_en: Tokyo Buddhist Youth Union in Japan

70권 호.title_kr: 원효는 시대의 한계를 넘어섰는가 - ‘女人不生’에 대한 박태원의 번역을 비판함 -
70권 호.title_en: Could Wonhyo Overcome the Limitation of the Times  - Critique on the Park, Taewon’s Translation of the “Women and the disabled are not reborn”-
70권 호.abstract_kr: 원효의 󰡔무량수경종요󰡕에는 세친의 󰡔정토론󰡕으로부터 “女人及根缺, 二乘種不生”이라는 구절이 인용되어 있다. 근래 원효의 저술을 상세하게 주석하면서 번역한 박태원은 이 구절을 옮김에 있어서 종래의 번역들과는 달리 “여성이나 신체의 결핍[에 대한차별]과 ‘[성문聲聞, 연각緣覺] 두 부류의 수행자’(二乘) 종류가 생겨나지 않는다네”라고 하였다. 원문에 없는 ‘[에 대한 차별]’을 번역자인 박태원 스스로 부가한 것이다.과연, 정토에는 여성이 없는가? 여성이 있는데 차별만은 없는가? 박태원은 후자를 주장하고 있다. 그러면서 그렇게 옮겨야 하는 이유로서 원효는 그러한 차별의 철학을 갖고 있지 않았기 때문이라 하였다.박태원은 이 문제를 다룸에 있어서 비평가적 주장을 앞세울 뿐, 학자적 엄밀성을 방기한 듯이 보인다. 그러나 필자는 바로 이 문제를 다룸에 있어서 일단은 텍스트에 대한 온전한 추적이 필요하다고 보았다. 즉 세친에서부터 담란을 거쳐, 원효에 이르기까지 해석의 역사를 살펴야 한다는 것이다. 그 결과 세친에서부터 담란, 그리고 원효에 이르기까지 일관되게 “정토에는 여성의 체(體)와 명(名) 모두 존재하지 않는다”는 데 의견을 같이하고 있었음을 알 수 있었다.그러므로 ‘여성 차별’과 관련하여 세친과 담란이 비판 받아야 한다면, 원효 역시 비판받아야 하는 것이다. 원효만은 오류가 없다. 시대의 한계를 넘어서 있다는 주장은 엄밀한 학문적 주장은 아님을 알 수 있었다. 그러한 전제 없이 원효의 텍스트를 허심탄회하게 읽어가면서, 혹시라도 오류가 있다고 한다면 그것은 그대로 비판하고 극복하는 것이 원효를 올바로 이해하고 선양하는 작업이 될 수 있으리라.
70권 호.abstract_en: The purpose of this article is to criticize Park Taewon’s translation of the phrase “There aren’t women and the disabled in the Pure Land” in Wonhyo’s Doctrinal Essentials of the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life(Muryangsugyeongjongyo). Compared to prior translaters, Prof. Park translated its phrase into  “There aren’t (the discrimination against) Women and the disabled in the Pure Land”.Although, I agree with his sense of equality between men and women, his translation is a misunderstanding of his phrase. Because he ignored  historical speculations about Pure Land Buddhism’s view of women. Vasubandhu and Tanluan had common views on the existence of women in the Pure Land in their (Sukhāvatīvyūha-)Upadeśa and (Sukhāvatīvyūha-)Upadeśa-Bhāṣya. It is that there aren’t not only its name but also its body in the Pure Land.Suceeding to their standpoints, Wonhyo also showed his viewpoints that there aren’t women’s name and body in the Pure Land in his Doctrinal Essentials of the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life(Muryangsugyeongjongyo) and Commentary Book on the Sūtra of Amitābhā by Buddha(Bulseolamitagyeongso).So I ’d like to point out that contrary to the translation of “There aren’t Women and the disabled in the Pure Land” is correct, that of “There aren’t (the discrimination against) Women and the disabled in the Pure Land” is incorrect.If we have to criticize Vasubandhu and Tanluan for having an anachronistic view of women, we must also criticize Wonhyo. They had same thought on women’s existence in the Pure Land. I can’t agree that only Wonhyo could overcome his limitations of the times. Wonhyo also lived in the same context.But we have to think about whether Prof. Park’s evaluation on Pure Land Buddhism in worldly or not. It will be my next theme.
keywords_en: Doctrinal Essentials of the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life(Muryangsugyeongjongyo)

70권 호.title_kr: 화쟁의 원류로서의 교판 - 사유구조의 연속성을 중심으로-
70권 호.title_en: The Doctrinal Classification as the Origin of Hwajaeng : Focusing on the Continuity of Cognitive Structures
70권 호.abstract_kr: This paper explores the continuous cognitive structures present in East Asian Buddhist texts, specifically the simultaneous affirmation and denial of the logically contradictory propositions that "each doctrine is differentiated" and "all doctrines are indiscriminate." In Wonhyo's Yŏlbanjongnyo (涅槃宗要), the concluding section extensively appropriates Jingying Huiyan's Zhongjingjiaojiyi (衆經敎迹義), presenting the doctrinal discourses of the Southern and Northern dynasty as opposing extremes. He articulates the idea that "if one clings to one extreme, all is wrong; if one does not cling, all is correct," thereby advocating the principle of Hwajaeng.Both Jingying Huiyan's Zhongjingjiaojiyi and its source text Fashang’s Jiaojiyi, propose the Liuqiu’s Sectional view and the Bodhiruci’s monolithic view on the Buddha’s teaching as opposing extremes. They aim to simultaneously affirm and deny the views that "all doctrines are gradual" and "all doctrines are ultimate" through an analysis of the texts and the positions of the Buddha as the speaker and sentient beings as the audience.Liuqiu, known for advocating the Sectional view Buddha’s teaching, presents the teachings of sudden (頓) and gradual (漸) as opposing extremes. In his work Wuliangyijing-shu (無量義經序), he asserts that both the sudden and the gradual teachings cannot be schematized. According to Liuqiu, though the Wuliangyijing is considered to be belong to the category of gradual (漸), it is mere a skillful means of the Buddha. He argues that since the core teaching of the Wuliangyijing is the formless (無相), it can be rightly considered as representing the ultimate realization of sudden teachings.In Conclusion, the East Asian Buddhist thinkers, despite their contextual and methodological differences, share a tendency to frame previous discussions as opposing extremes while seeking to overcome and unify these two perspectives. This underscores the necessity of a broader view of East Asian Buddhism for a more accurate assessment of the significance of Wonhyo’s thought.
70권 호.abstract_en: 본고는 원효 화쟁 논법의 특징, 즉 ‘각각의 교설은 차등적이다’라는 명제와 ‘모든 교설은 무차별이다’라는 논리적으로 모순된 명제에 대한 동시 부정과 동시 긍정이 그 전 세대의 동아시아 불교문헌에서도 나타나고 있었음을 고찰하였다.원효의 󰡔열반종요󰡕는 말미의 ｢명교적｣에서 정영사 혜원의 ｢중경교적의｣를 대거 차용해 남조와 북조의 교판론을 양 극단의 설로 제시하고 “한 극단에 집착하면 모두 틀리고 집착하지 않는다면 모두 옳다”는 화쟁의 사상을 설파하고 있다.정영사 혜원의 ｢중경교적의｣와 그 모본인 법상 ｢교적의｣는 돈점 7계5시교와 일음교를 양 극단의 설로 제시하고, 경전의 화자인 붓다와 청자인 중생의 입장, 그리고 문헌 분석을 통해 ‘모든 교설이 단계적’이라는 관점과 ‘모든 교설이 궁극적’이라는 입장의 동시 긍정과 동시 부정을 꾀하고 있다.돈점 7계5시교를 주창했다고 알려진 유규의 교판론은 돈교와 점교를 양 극단의 설로 제시하고 있다. 유규의 ｢무량의경서｣는 돈교와 점교를 도식적으로 파악할 수 있는 것이 아님을 주장한다. 󰡔무량의경󰡕은 7계교에 속하는 것이기는 하지만 이것은 어디까지나 붓다의 비밀스러운 방편이며 󰡔무량의경󰡕의 핵심 교설이 무상(無相)인 이상 궁극적인 깨달음을 의미하는 돈교의 설이라고 해도 옳다는 것이다.이처럼 그 맥락이나 방법론적인 차이에도 불구하고, 동아시아 불교 논사들은 전대의 논의를 양 극단으로 삼고 두 관점의 극복과 회통을 꾀하고 있다는 점에서는 동일하다. 원효의 사상이 지니는 의의를 보다 정확히 평가하기 위해서는 동아시아 불교라는 더 넓은 견지가 필요한 이유이다.

70권 호.title_kr: 지공의 고려에서의 위상과 나옹의 지공 계승 - 지공의 사리와 보스톤미술관 사리구 문제까지 -
70권 호.title_en: The status of Jigong(指空) in Goryeo and his succession by Naong(懶翁) - centering on Jigong's Sarira and the Sarira case in Boston Fine Art Museum -
70권 호.abstract_kr: 미국 보스턴미술관에는 1939년 일본의 야마나카 상회에서 구입한 높이 22.2㎝로 된 ‘은제도금 라마탑형 사리구’가 전시되어 있다. 이 사리구에는 작은 8각형 사리구 5개가 봉안되어 있다. 이를 소위 ‘3여래如來 2조사祖師’라고 하는데, 이 중 사리는 유물이 아니므로 조계종의 요청으로 2024년 4월 16일에 한국에 반환되었다. 이를 계기로 지공과 나옹의 한국 불교사적인 위상에 대두 이유에 대한 관심이 모아지고 있다.본 고는 인도 승려인 지공이 고려불교에 강인한 인상을 남길 수 있던 이유로 배경적인 2가지와 불교적인 2가지에 주목했다. 배경으로서의 2가지는 첫째, 원 간섭기에는 고려인의 위치가 중국 한족보다 높아서 중화주의가 작동하지 않았다는 점. 둘째, 지공이 원의 제6대 황제인 진종晉宗의 어향사御香使 신분으로 고려에 왔다는 점이다. 불교적인 2가지는 지공의 주장에 따르면, 지공의 가계는 부계로는 붓다의 혈족血族이며, 모계로는 달마의 혈족이라는 점이다.또 지공은 무생계無生戒라는 대승불교의 계율戒律을 주된 교화 수단으로 삼았는데, 이는 신분과 지위를 가리지 않고 다수를 한꺼번에 교화할 수 있는 방법이었다. 이로 인해 지공은 고려불교에 막대한 영향을 행사하게 된다.이 지공의 수제자로서 신돈의 몰락과 함께 부각 되는 게 나옹이다. 이런 점에서 공민왕의 나옹에 대한 왕사 책봉에는 지공의 영향이 강하게 작용한다고 하겠다. 이러한 지공과 나옹의 관계를 나타내주는 유물이 바로 보스톤미술관의 사리구이다.
70권 호.abstract_en: The Boston Fine Art Museum in the United States exhibits a 22.2 cm tall ‘silver-plated Rama tower-shaped sarira case’ purchased from Yamanaka Trading Company of Japan in 1939. This sarira case enshrines 5 small octagonal reliquaries, which are called the ‘3 Tathagatas(如來) and 2 Patriarchs(祖師).’ Since the sarira is not an artifact, it was returned to Korea on April 16, 2024 at the request of the Jogyejong Order. This has increased the interests in the status of Jigong and Naong in Korean Buddhist history.This study focuses on 2 backgrounds and 2 Buddhist reasons why Jigong, an Indian monk, was able to leave a strong impression on Goryeo Buddhism. The 2 background factors are: first, during the Yuan intervention, the status of Goryeo people was higher than that of the Chinese Han people, so Sinocentrism did not work; Second, Jigong came to Goryeo as the incense priest of the 6th emperor Jinzong(晉宗) of the Yuan Dynasty. The 2 Buddhist factors are: according to Jigong’s claims, his lineage was the blood relative of Buddha on his father’s side and the blood relative of Dharma on his mother’s side.In addition, Jigong used the Mahayana Buddhist śīla-vinaya of non-birth precept(無生戒) as his main teaching method, which was a method that he could teach many people at once regardless of their status or positions. As a result, Jigong came to have a huge influence on Goryeo Buddhism.As a Jigong's disciple, Naong emerged along with the downfall of Shin Don. In this respect, Jigong's influence must have been strong in King Gongmin's appointment of Naong as the royal preceptor. The relic that shows this relationship between Jigong and Naong is the sarira reliquary in the Boston Fine Art Museum.

71권 호.title_kr: 현곡 김잉석의 보조 연구에 대한 소고
71권 호.title_en: Reflections on Kim Ying-Seok's research on Jinul
71권 호.abstract_kr: 현곡 김잉석은 승려로서의 삶을 멈추고 세상 속으로 뛰어들어 근대 한국 불교학을 정초하고, 불교를 이전과 다른 새로운 근대적 방식으로 연구하고자 하였다. 본고는 그의 연구물 가운데서도 보조국사 지눌에 대한 저술들을 중심으로 고찰해 보고자 한다. 김잉석은 승려로서의 체험을 바탕으로 지눌의 수증론을 해설하고, 지눌이 기존 화엄학자들의 틀에 갇히지 않고 이통현을 발굴한 것에 대해 극찬을 아끼지 않는다. 특히 징관이 법성종 안에 선종을 포괄하고, 선을 화엄보다 낮은 단계에 두는 것에 대해 예리한 비판을 가하는 지눌의 모습은 김잉석에게 강한 인상을 남겼다. 그러나 김잉석의 화엄학이 지눌에게 어떻게 적용되는가 하는 면에 대해서는 앞으로 좀 더 연구해야 할 필요성이 있다. 김잉석은 시종일관 따뜻한 시선으로 지눌을 바라보지만, 지눌이 선사로서 징관을 보는 관점과 김잉석이 화엄학자로서 징관을 보는 관점에는 서로 다른 부분이 드러난다. 또한 김잉석은 지눌이 징관을 평가하면서 보이는 미묘한 태도를 깊이 표현하지 못한 부분도 있는 것으로 보인다. 이러한 면들을 고찰하면서 본고는 앞으로 근대불교 지식인들이 느꼈던 시대적 압력과 서구 학문을 바라보는 복합적 의식을 토대로 김잉석의 학문적 자취와 노력이 연구되어야 한다고 조망하였다.

71권 호.title_kr: 돈황본  『수심요론(修心要論) 』의 신(信)과 신행(信行) 연구
71권 호.title_en: A Study on Faith and Practice in Xiuxinyaolun (Treatise on the Essentials of Cultivating the Mind)
71권 호.abstract_kr: This study examines the early manuscript P.3664 of Xiuxinyaolun (修心要論), a key text from the formative period of early Chan Buddhism. The study analyzes the concept of faith (信) presented in the text, along with Buddhist faith-based practices that were widely practiced in China at the time but evaluated differently in the treatise. Through this analysis, the study aims to explore the characteristics of early Chan Buddhist thought.Xiuxinyaolun regards the true Buddha as the Dharma itself and exclusively associates it with the mind. Thus, it presents a mind-centered theory of Buddha-nature and enlightenment, where the practitioner's pure mind is the true Buddha, and attaining enlightenment is achieved through maintaining the mind (守心).Additionally, Xiuxinyaolun offers a distinct perspective on Buddhist faith-based practices widely practiced during its time. In China, practices such as reciting the names of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, visualizing Buddhas and their lands in meditation, and ascetic practices as part of the Bodhisattva path were prevalent. These practices were based on faith in the existence of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as their reward bodies, scriptural accounts of their deeds, and belief in their attainment of the Bodhisattva path and its fruition. However, Xiuxinyaolun, prioritizing maintaining one’s mind as the means to enlightenment, argues that practices based on faith in the reward-body Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot free one from the cycle of birth and death and may even become an obstacle to nirvana.Furthermore, in Mahāyāna Buddhism, stupas (śarīra stupas and scripture stupas) and scriptures were regarded as the Dharma-body Buddha, and this understanding was widely accepted in the development of Chinese Buddhism, as seen in the construction of stupas and the advancement of Buddhist teachings. However, Xiuxinyaolun asserts that the One Vehicle exists solely within the true suchness of the mind. From this perspective, the merit of stupa construction and the content of scriptures are merely skillful means for sentient beings, while attaining Buddhahood depends solely on maintaining the mind.Accordingly, unlike contemporary commentaries, Xiuxinyaolun quotes Mahāyāna scriptures but does not prioritize any particular text. It also does not mention the recitation and memorization of scriptures —a defining characteristic of Mahāyāna practice— and instead reinterprets quoted passages in alignment with the practice of maintaining the mind. Therefore, the concept of faith in Xiuxinyaolun reveals the distinctive belief system of Chan Buddhism, setting it apart from other Buddhist schools, and highlights the characteristics of mind-centered practice based on this faith.
keywords_en: Treatise on the Essentials of Cultivating the Mind

71권 호.title_kr: 『범망경』 십중계(十重戒)의 범죄 구성요건에 관한 연구 – 신라 승려들의 인(因)·연(緣)·법(法)·업(業) 이해를 중심으로 -
71권 호.title_en: A Study on the Elements of Crimes in the Ten grave Precepts of the Brahma’s Net Sutra:  Focusing on the Understanding of Cause, Condition, Method of conduct, and Completion of a case by Silla Monks Wonhyo, Uijeok, Seungjang, and Taehyun
71권 호.abstract_kr: This study analyzes the perspectives of the Silla monks Wonhyo (元曉), Uijeok (義寂), Seungjang (勝莊), and Taehyun (太賢) on the four elements of crime in the Ten grave Precepts of the Brahma’s Net Sutra (Ch. Fanwang jing, 梵網經): “Cause” (因), “Condition” (緣), “Method of conduct” (法), and “Completion of a case” (業).Wonhyo considers various texts, including the Mahāsāṃghika Vinaya (摩訶僧祇律) , while Uijeok, Seungjang, and Taehyun place significant emphasis on the five conditions of the “Ten Evil Acts” (十惡業道) in volume 59 of the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra(Ch. Yuqie shidi lun, 瑜伽師地論) when interpreting the elements of crime. Rather than referring to the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra or its commentary on the Bodhisattva Path (菩薩地), they focus on these five conditions: “affair” (事象), “ideation” (想), “intention” (欲樂), “affliction” (煩惱), and “complete method” (方便究竟).Uijeok exclusively applies these conditions when explaining the element of “Condition” (緣) in the Brahma’s Net Sutra. In contrast, Seungjang largely disregards the structural elements of the Brahma’s Net Sutra and predominantly relies on the five conditions from volume 59 of the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra. Uijeok incorporates these five conditions to interpret the Brahma’s Net Sutra’s elements of “Cause”, “Condition”, “Method of conduct”, and “Completion of a case”, while also offering his own interpretation. Notably, he subdivides the “complete method” (方便究竟) into “method” (方便) and “completion” (究竟) and alters “intention” (yule, 欲樂) to “intention” (yiyao, 意樂).The analysis of the elements of a crime serves as a foundational framework for ethical value judgments regarding the interpretation of actions and motives. Within the exegetical tradition of the Brahma’s Net Sutra, which remains influential to this day, key components—Cause”, “Condition”, “Method of conduct”, and “Completion of a case”—have already been systematically analyzed. The discussions on the grave crimes in the Brahma’s Net Sutra, a representative text of the Mahāyāna Bodhisattva Precepts, are expected to contribute to the establishment of East Asian Buddhist ethics as a scholarly field.

71권 호.title_kr: 『구사론』 제9장에 대한 진제와 현장의 한역용어 비교: 중국역경원칙에 따른 음역과 의역 비교
71권 호.title_en: A Comparative Study of the Chinese Terminology Between Paramartha’s and Xuanzang’s in the 9th Chapter of the Abhidharmakoshabhasya, in Light of the Translation Principles in Chinese Buddhism
71권 호.abstract_kr: This is a comparative study of the Chinese terminology made by Paramartha(眞諦) and Xuanzang(玄奘) in the 9th chapter of the Abhidharmakoshabhasya(俱舍論).According to the traditional Chinese principles of translation, the transliteration(音譯) corresponds to the phonetic transliteration-in-the-five-cases(五不翻) which means the transliteration should be applied for the exceptional five cases where the literal translation can’t convey the original meanings exactly; while the literal paraphrase(義譯) corresponding to the literal translation(正翻) and the figurative translation(義翻). In light of these traditional translation rules of the Chinese Buddhism, I discussed the characteristic features of Chinese terms used by Paramartha and Xuanzang by dividing them into two groups of phonetic transliteration and semantic literal translation.In this survey, I found that their translation generally coincide with the traditional principles of translation. Although Xuanzang is known to have established the principles of the transliteration, but there must have been a sort of practice of translation before him judging from this coincidence. Anyway, the principles of translation were eventually presented as a solution to overcome the dilemmas of translation itself, there are slight differences in their actual application of the rules. Compared with Paramartha’s, Xuanzang’s has more literal terms(義譯), notably in proper nouns (as in ‘毘伽羅論師’→‘記論者’). Xuanzang seems to have preferred the literal translation to transliteration, to make it easier and clearer for the average readers to understand the meaning of the original text.However, despite Xuanzang’s ground-breaking translation with his own new terms, it’s quite surprising that his terminology coincide with Paramartha’s than expected, which means he must have referred to Paramartha’s whose terminology is basically comprised of older terms(舊譯). And it also indicates that each of them employed the older terms that were verified throughout the history. The fact that his terminology has many parts in common with the Paramartha’s reveals that the history of translation from Sanskrit into Chinese of Buddhist scriptures in Chinese Buddhism was the result of such a collective intelligence accumulated over a long period of time.

71권 호.title_kr: 목우가풍의 존재론적 위상과 계승 - 불교 정신문화 교류를 중심으로 -
71권 호.title_en: The Ontological Significance and Transmission of Mok-u Ga-pung  - Focusing on Exchanges in Buddhist Spiritual Culture -
71권 호.abstract_kr: This paper delves into the potential of the Jeong-Hye Gyeol-sa (定慧結社) spirit and Mok-u-ga-pung (牧牛歌風) of the late Goryeo dynasty to build peace in contemporary South Korean society, which is grappling with severe internal and external conflicts (political polarization, economic inequality, generational and gender conflicts, low birthrate and super-aged society) and an unstable international situation.  Specifically, by reinterpreting Bojo Jijul's (普照知訥) activities within the context of conflict transformation, this paper examines the discourse surrounding how religious leaders and practitioners of religious policy should approach religion, and simultaneously engages in ongoing discussions about the role of religion in domestic and international conflicts and disputes.Utilizing the five functional frameworks of religion (community, teachings, spirituality, practice, discourse) proposed by Owen Frazer and Richard Friedli's research at the Center for Security Studies (CSS) in Zurich, Switzerland, this analysis explores how Bojo Jijul's Jeong-Hye Gyeol-sa and Mok-u-ga-pung align with these frameworks and contribute to conflict resolution and social integration. This demonstrates that Mok-u-ga-pung serves as a crucial example of how religion can function not as a mere "divider" in social conflict, but rather as a "connector" for peace.Furthermore, throughout the 20th and early 21st centuries, whenever Korean Buddhism faced critical crises within the religious order and broader society, new forms of Jeong-Hye Gyeol-sa emerged, contributing to conflict resolution and social cohesion. This prompts reflection among religious leaders and practitioners on the role of religion within the religious order and the national community.  This paper revisits Bojo's spirit of communal practice, arguing that its spiritual and cultural legacy should be inherited and developed through diverse religious roles to foster harmony and integration within the community.

71권 호.title_kr: 중국불교에 나타난 관세음보살에 대한 관점 - 도생, 법운, 천태지의를 중심으로 -
71권 호.title_en: Perspectives on Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in Chinese Buddhism: Focusing on Daosaeng, Fayun, and Tiantai Zhiyi
71권 호.abstract_kr: In this article, in order to examine the viewpoints of Guanshiyin(觀世音) Pusa(菩薩) that is, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in Chinese buddhism, we look at the viewpoints of Daosheng(道生), Fayun(法雲), and Tiantai Zhiyi(天台智顗). In chapter 2, I briefly introduces the contents of Guanshiyin pusa pumen pin(觀世音菩薩普門品) in the Lotus Sutra. In chapter 3, I examines the viewpoints of Daosheng and Fayun. Daosheng(道生) approaches by dividing ‘Guanshiyin(觀世音)’ and ‘Pumen(普門)’. So, Guanshiyin(觀世音)’ is a being with a heart to save all living beings, and ‘Pumen(普門)’ refers to a mysterious action to save all living beings widely. This influenced the viewpoints of Tiantai Zhiyi. And Fayun(法雲) says that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva saves sentient beings by contemplating their voice(oral karma), physical karma, and intentional karma, and also saves them by contemplating these three karma comprehensively. This argument also influenced the viewpoints of Tiantai Zhiyi(天台智顗). In chapter 4, I examines the viewpoints of Tiantai Zhiyi. While being influenced by Daosaeng and Fayun's viewpoints, Tiantai Zhiyi(天台智顗) presents his own independent viewpoint. It appears in the interpretation of each letter of ‘Guanshiyin(觀世音)’ and ‘Pumen(普門)’. According to this interpretation, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva is a being who contemplates reality, and all sentient beings who listen to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s teachings or have relationships become Buddha, and the teachings that Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva presents are perfect teachings and the middle way of teachings.

71권 호.title_kr: 도섬(道暹)의 생애와 저작  - 기초 연구 및 진위 검토 -
71권 호.title_en: The Life and Works of Daoxian : A Preliminary Study and Examination of Authenticity
71권 호.abstract_kr: Daoxian (道暹) was an 8th-century Chinese monk of the Tiantai school who authored several extant works. Based on the frequency of their citations, Daoxian is considered to have significantly influenced later Buddhist thought. However, research on Daoxian remains insufficient, leaving many aspects of his life and ideas unclear. This paper aims to contribute to foundational research on Daoxian by collecting historical records, reconstructing his life, and re-evaluating the authenticity of the works traditionally attributed to him.Biographical records about Daoxian are fragmented and lack a cohesive narrative. References to his life and activities appear sporadically in limited texts, such as his own Fahuawenjufuzhengji (『法華文句輔正記』), Zhiyuan's (智圓, 976–1022) Weimojinglueshuchiyuji (『維摩經略疏垂裕記』), Zanning's (賛寧) Songgaosengzhuan (『宋高僧傳』), and Zhipan's (志磐) Fozutongji (『佛祖統紀』). Due to these limitations, many aspects of Daoxian's life remain unclear. However, upon closer examination, it has been confirmed that Daoxian was a direct disciple of Zhanran（湛然, 711–782） and contributed to the inheritance and development of Zhanran's teachings.A synthesis of prior research and catalog sources reveals eight works comprising 39 volumes attributed to Daoxian. However, discrepancies in authorial attributions between catalogs and inconsistencies across different versions of the same catalog prompted further scrutiny. After careful examination of these catalogs and related materials, the following four works were confirmed as authentic compositions by Daoxian: 1.Fahuawenjufuzhengji (『法華文句輔正記』), 2.Niepanjingshusiji (『涅槃經疏私記』), 3.Weimoxuanshuji (『維摩玄疏記』), 4.Weimoshusiji (『維摩疏私記』). The other works traditionally attributed to Daoxian were found to be either of questionable authenticity or misattributions of texts authored by others. Conversely, cases were identified where Daoxian’s works were erroneously attributed to other authors.

71권 호.title_kr: 약카(Yakkha) 신앙의 불교적 해석과 수용 - Āḷavakavaṇṇāna를 중심으로 -
71권 호.title_en: Revisiting the Yakkha Narrative as Described  in the Āḷavakavaṇṇāna
71권 호.abstract_kr: Yakkha is a tree spirit that symbolizes abundance and prosperity among ancient Indians, and has been worshiped as a cult. For the Brahman tradition, and other religious traditions such as Buddhism and Jainism, the Yakkha worship was absorbed and reinterpreted in their own form. In the case of Buddhist tradition, Yakkha, reinterpreted from a Buddhist perspective, emerges through vast commentary literature. In Buddhist literature, Yakkha is mainly described as a unique character with both good and evil through narratives. They are sometimes depicted as monsters hiding in trees and cannibalizing, or as sincere Buddhists who go on a trip to listen to the Buddha's teachings. In the commentary, Yakkha was depicted as a tyrant with a huge palace and maids, not a tree spirit. They have cannibalism, as well as transformation and flight ability, and they were like tribes, so they had different names, abilities, and tendencies. In particular, Alavaka Yakka is described as an attractive villain who continues a macho but delicate psychological change despite being violent. From this research, it was also possible to confirm the process of Buddhist tradition absorbing folk beliefs at the time, the hermeneutic intentions and methods of extensive commentary literature, and the archetype and development of Buddhist narratives.

71권 호.title_kr: 탑돌이에 나타난 우요(右繞)의 상징과 의미
71권 호.title_en: The Symbol and Meaning on the Right-Handed Circulation of Stupa
71권 호.abstract_kr: Culture, the result of human thought, can show different aspects depending on the region and era, even if it is the same phenomenon. How has Korean Buddhism, which has been absolutely influenced by Chinese Buddhism, accepted and transmitted the point where Indian and Chinese cultures collided? A representative example is hand seals. Even though it is called Zen meditation seals, unlike the right hand on top of the left hand in Indian Buddhism, the left hand is placed on top in Chinese Buddhism. Among these, the record related to the conflict remains in the “Samundanbokron (沙門袒服論)” in Volume 5 of Hongmyeongjip. Although this is a comprehensive and ambiguous question, if we consider various factors depending on the case, the answer to this question will probably not be a uniform answer, but rather a variety of answers depending on the situation. On the surface, Korean pagoda circling may seem like a simple form of continuously circling a pagoda, but its understanding, interpretation, and meaning are by no means simple. First, the following questions may be raised: Why do we need to circle a pagoda? Second, how can we define the principles and certain forms of circling a pagoda? Next, we may ask: Who is the subject of the pagoda circling, the practitioner? What does pagoda circling mean to the practitioner? What is the ultimate goal of pagoda circling? This paper seeks to provide partial answers to these questions, while at the same time tracing the origins of the right-hand circling of a pagoda that is practiced in Korean Buddhism today.

71권 호.title_kr: 사찰음식에 관한 국내 연구 동향 분석
71권 호.title_en: Analysis of domestic research trends on temple food
71권 호.abstract_kr: Despite growing interest in temple food due to health and wellness trends, related research is limited. This study analyzes existing temple food research and suggests future directions. We examined 77 papers from the Research Information Sharing Service(RISS), analyzing trends by year, journal, researcher, and methodology. Language network analysis was also employed. Key findings include: temple food research emerged in 1994, peaking in 2015; major publishing journals are in food science and tourism; most papers are single-authored; quantitative methods, particularly surveys, dominate; and key themes include value, perception, satisfaction, and intention. The study identified four main research topics related to temple food through language network analysis, providing a foundation for future research in this field.

72권 호.title_kr: “한 마음”은 어떻게 세계의 기반이 되었는가      - 『기신론』의 일심 개념 성립에 대하여 -
72권 호.title_en: How Did“One Mind”Become the Basis of the World? - On the Formation of the Concept of One Mind in the Awakening of Faith -
72권 호.abstract_kr: This article undertakes a critical examination of prior scholarship claiming that the Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna (Dashengqixinlun, henceforth “Qixinlun”)’s doctrine of “one mind” (一心) was influenced by the thought of Sengwei (僧衛), a monk active in the early 5th century. To reassess this assertion, I have analyzed Shizhujinghanzhuxu (十住經含注序) ascribed to Sengwei, as well as the Buddhist texts composed in the Northern Dynasties of early 6th century, the region where the Qixinlun was compiled. The findings of this investigation are as follows.While the notion of “one mind” in the Daśabhūmika Sūtra does not necessarily signify a foundational ground of the phenomenal world, Sengwei’s interpretation presents “one mind” as the mind that functions as the origin of phenomenal existence. However, this appears to reflect not so much a close reading of the Daśabhūmika Sūtra itself as it does a broader mode of thought prevalent in Southern Chinese Buddhism at the time. Above all, the dualistic framework distinguishing “one mind” and “one dharma” in Sengwei’s system differs substantially from the ontological conception of “one mind” articulated in the Qixinlun.By contrast, the Shidijinglun (十地經論), translated in the sixth century in Northern China, explicitly identifies “one mind” with the ālayavijñāna, which is described as possessing a dual nature of purity and defilement. Furthermore, the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra (入楞伽經), translated by Bodhiruci—one of the leading translators and exegetes of the Northern Dynasties—along with his associated doctrinal formulations, clearly articulates a conceptual structure equating one mind with ālayavijñāna and tathāgatagarbha. This structure, as my research shows, is faithfully inherited in Chinese-authored texts from the same milieu. In light of the existence of such conceptually and geographically proximate sources, there appears to be little necessity to trace the doctrinal origins of the Qixinlun back to Sengwei, a figure of the preceding century. From this perspective, it is more plausible to regard the Qixinlun’s formulation of the “one mind” doctrine as having emerged from the interpretative horizon shaped by contemporary Chinese translations of Indian scriptures and their exegetical traditions.

In the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Abhidharmasamuccaya, and Mahāyānasaṃgraha, the concept of arthāntarābhiprāya(別義意趣) appears. It has previously been noted that the notion of arthāntarābhiprāya in the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra and Abhidharmasamuccaya are different from Mahāyānasamgraha. There are two differences. First, The scriptural passages cited as examples of arthāntarābhiprāya differ between the two groups of texts. Second, The passages in the former two works are generally understood to be based on the doctrine of the Three Natures (trisvabhāva), while the intention behind the passage in the Mahāyānasamgraha is ambiguous with regard to whether it aims to express the Three Natures.This paper examines the concept of arthāntarābhiprāya as it appears in each of these texts.  And as a result, I would like to add the following two differences to the existing differences that have already been pointed out. First, In the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra and Abhidharmasamuccaya, arthāntarā(別意) means hidden intention(密意), whereas in the Mahāyānasamgraha, it means a meaning that transcends language. Second, The passages cited in the former works is written with the intention of Three Natures, whereas the passage in the Mahāyānasamgraha is sentence that speaks in meaning of transcends language like Three Natures.Furthermore, this paper points out a similarity between the Mahāyānasaṃgraha and the Laṅkāvatārasūtra in terms of their perspectives on the Buddha’s words. That is, the Mahāyānasaṃgraha, by understanding arthāntarābhiprāya as a transcends language meaning, reflects a view of the Buddha’s words as comprising both linguistic and non-linguistic dimensions. This recognition is similarly found in the Laṅkāvatārasūtra, which distinguishes between the “doctrine of instruction” (deśanānaya) and the “doctrine of ultimate truth” (siddhāntanaya). Thus, both the Mahāyānasaṃgraha and the Laṅkāvatārasūtra show similarity in their understanding of the Buddha’s words.

72권 호.title_kr: 스리랑카 탈팟(Talpat) 전통과 필사본 연구(2) - 야자수 잎 가공과정과 필사작업을 중심으로 -
72권 호.title_en: Sri Lankan Talpat Tradition: Traditional Approach and Its Implications
72권 호.abstract_kr: This article analyses the Sri Lankan Palm-leaf Manuscript tradition called Talpat. Within Sri Lanka, the Talpat tradition has been preserved by a limited number of experts, while the traditional production process is gradually diminishing or undergoing simplification. However, this production process has become an important factor both in the ritual aspect of Sri Lankan Buddhism and in terms of folk beliefs or worships. This paper examines in detail through local data and researches the structure and characteristics of the manuscript production process whoch have been handed down only inside Sri Lanka. The process of making Talpat begins with collecting and processing palm leaves. This process only limited palm leaves on a designated date is a kind of religious ceremony that reflects the religious life of ancient Sri Lankans who respect nature and believe in the gods of the trees in them. The process of putting the collected leaves together with various medicinal ingredients, boiling, drying and cutting them into standard sizes contains the desire to safely preserve and transmit the manuscript, which will become a Buddhist script in the future, and is also a very example of the advanced scientific level of ancient Sri Lanka. Transcribing on those processed palm leaves is done only by experienced professionals who have gone through a certain period of education. In particular, the Talpat tradition has various unique letter-forms (Akshara), which seems to have been selected according to the scribe and the region of production and the type of manuscript. After that, the coloring and finishing works that make the transcribed letters stand out will be followed by traditional rituals and procedures. Apart from the advanced printing techniques of modern society, this understanding of the Talpat tradition provides a new approach to understanding Sri Lankan unique Buddhist culture.

72권 호.title_kr: 초기 경전에 나타난 언어적 형성작용(vacī-saṅkhāra)의 수행론적 의의  - vitakka의 활용을 중심으로-
72권 호.title_en: The Practical Implications of Linguistic Formation (Vacī-saṅkhāra) in Early Buddhist Scriptures: Focusing on the Utilization of Vitakka
72권 호.abstract_kr: This study aims to explore the concept of linguistic formation (vacī-saṅkhāra) as presented in early Buddhist scriptures and to clarify its practical significance from the perspective of the utilization of vitakka. Moving beyond existing research, which has primarily focused on the conceptual meaning of vitakka or its comparison with Yoga traditions, this study demonstrates that vitakka, a key component of linguistic formation, can serve both as a source of defilements and as a crucial meditative tool for practice and liberation.Linguistic formation is not merely a verbal act; rather, it constitutes an intentional psychological process composed of vitakka (initial application of mind) and vicāra (sustained application of mind). Vitakka itself exhibits a dynamic duality, capable of leading to either wholesome or unwholesome states depending on the practitioner’s intention and mental condition. When unwholesome, vitakka, in combination with craving (taṇhā) and ignorance (avijjā), develops into proliferation (papañca), which manifests as multiple layers of defilements, ranging from gross actions to subtle forms of self-clinging. In contrast, wholesome vitakka, when guided by right intention and wisdom, becomes an essential factor in jhāna (meditative absorption), aligns with right thought (sammā-saṅkappa) in the Noble Eightfold Path, and positively contributes to the realization of the Four Noble Truths and the emergence of the factors of awakening (bojjhaṅga).This research presents concrete scriptural evidence for both the wholesome and unwholesome dimensions of vitakka, and provides an analysis of five specific meditative methods from early scriptures for skillfully managing unwholesome vitakka and cultivating wholesome vitakka. In conclusion, a holistic understanding of linguistic formation, together with its core element vitakka, offers practical guidelines for the purification of mind and the perfection of wisdom in early Buddhist practice, ultimately leading to liberation. Academically, this study contributes by highlighting the pivotal role of vitakka in mediating the interaction between nāma-rūpa (mind-and-matter) and by providing an integrated understanding of mind and body within early Buddhist meditation. Future research is encouraged to investigate practical methodologies for applying the utilization of vitakka in contemporary psychotherapy and meditation programs.

73권 호.title_kr: 한국불교에서 계율 전통의 전개에 대한 소고
73권 호.title_en: A Study on the Development of Vinaya Traditions in Korean Buddhism
73권 호.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 한국불교에서 구족계 수계제도가 성립하고 전개되는 과정에대한 통시적인 검토이다. 불교의 계율은 출가 공동체의 정체성과 질서를규정하는 핵심 장치이며, 그 가운데 구족계 수계의식은 출가 수행자를 승가의 정식 구성원으로 승인하는 절차로 시대적 상황 속에서 교단 운영의근간이 되어 왔다.본고에서는 율장에 보이는 부처님 당시 구족계 관련 기록을 출발점으로삼은 뒤, 곧바로 한국의 삼국시대, 고려 · 조선시대, 근현대 세 시기의 구분을 토대로 그 제도적 전개를 살펴보았다. 먼저 삼국시대에는 고구려의승관제 운영과 백제 겸익의 율장 번역, 신라의 계단 설치를 통해 구족계의제도적 기반이 마련되었으며, 이는 한국불교 율학 전통의 기원이다.고려시대에는 승록사를 통한 국가적 관리 속에서 승려의 신분을 공인한제도로 구족계가 정착하였다. 그리고 조선시대에는 도첩제를 통해 출가 자격이 국가 통제 아래 놓인 한편, 군역 회피와 면역 등의 문제 속에서도 승단은 자체적인 의식과 전승을 통해 정체성을 유지하였다.근현대에는 일제강점기 사찰령과 대처승 문제로 계율 전통이 흔들렸지만, 환성 지안의 순교 이후 서상수계를 토대로 계맥을 되살릴 수 있었고, 마침내 1962년 통합종단이 계단법을 제정함으로써 구족계의 현대적 제도화가 이루어졌다.이상의 고찰은 구족계 수계제도가 단순한 출가의례를 넘어 교단 정체성과 사회적 위상을 규정하는 역사적 지표였음을 밝히며, 나아가 한국불교계율 전통의 현대적 의의를 한데 모아 재조명해 본 결과이다.
73권 호.abstract_en: This study examines the formation and development of the full ordination (具足戒, Bhikṣu/Bhikṣuṇī precepts) system in Korean Buddhism from a diachronic perspective. Precepts in Buddhism serve as the essential framework that regulates the identity and ethical order of the monastic community, and among them, the full ordination ritual has functioned as the central procedure that officially admits an aspirant into the Saṅgha.Beginning with records in the early Vinaya texts from the Buddha’s time, this paper traces the institutional development of ordination through the Three Kingdoms, the Goryeo and Joseon dynasties, and the modern period. In the Three Kingdoms, the establishment of the monastic office in Goguryeo, the Vinaya translation by Gyeomik of Baekje, and the ordination platforms of Silla provided the institutional foundation of Korean Vinaya tradition.During the Goryeo dynasty, the Office of Monastic Affairs (Seungnoksa) institutionalized the recognition of monastic status, integrating the full ordination system into the framework of state governance. In the Joseon dynasty, Confucian state ideology suppressed Buddhism, the monk registration system (Doch’eopje) placed ordination under state control, yet the monastic order preserved its identity through ritual transmission.In the modern era, despite distortions under the Japanese colonial Temple Ordinance and the married clergy controversy, the Vinaya transmission was maintained through the lineage of Hwanseong Jian and the Seosang ordination. With the establishment of the unified Jogye Order in 1962 and the enactment of the Ordinance on Ordination Platforms, the system was reorganized into a modern institutional framework.This study demonstrates that the full ordination in Korea was not merely a ritual of monastic initiation but a historical index that reflects the identity of the Buddhist order and its relation to society and the state, thereby explaining to a renewed understanding of the contemporary significance of Vinaya tradition in Korean Buddhism.

73권 호.title_en: A Comparative Study of Gobul Chongrim and Kaya Chongrim in the Post-Liberation Period
73권 호.abstract_kr: presented at the inaugural academic conference commemorating the establishment of the Gobul Chongrim Research Institute at Baegyangsa Temple in November 2024. It aims to examine the activities and significance of Baegyangsa’s Gobul Chongrim by comparing it with the Kaya Chongrim established in the same post-liberation period.The discussion focuses on three main issues.First, it explores the historical background behind the founding of Buddhist chongrim(comprehensive monastic training complexes) in the post-liberation period, particularly examining how Ven. Manam Jongheon, founder of Gobul Chongrim, and Ven. Hyobong Haknul, founder of Kaya Chongrim, respectively understood the raison d’être of a chongrim.Second, it investigates the spiritual practices undertaken by Manam prior to founding Gobul Chongrim, the process that led to its establishment, and the nature and activities that characterized this institution.Third, it analyzes the spiritual training and developmental process of Hyobong in founding Kaya Chongrim, along with the characteristics and religious activities of this community.Following the liberation from Japanese colonial rule, the Korean Buddhist community sought various directions amid social confusion. These efforts played a crucial role in shaping the identity of modern Korean Buddhism. The establishments of Gobul Chongrim and Kaya Chongrim represented movements led by senior meditation monks to create exemplary and comprehensive Buddhist training centers. Despite their historical significance, they have received less scholarly attention compared to the Bongamsa kyŏlsa. This study is meaningful in that it reexamines the existing understanding of Buddhist activities during Korea’s post-liberation period.
73권 호.abstract_en: 본 논문은 2024년 11월 백양사 ‘고불총림연구원’의 개원 기념 학술대회에서 발표한 논문을 수정 보완 한 것이다. 백양사 고불총림의 활동 및 그의의를 드러내기 위한 목적 아래 해방공간의 고불총림과 가야총림에 대해비교한 글이다.본 논문에서 다루고 있는 쟁점은 크게 세 가지 문제이다.첫째는 해방 공산에서 불교계가 총림을 설립한 배경과 함께 고불총림을설립한 만암 종헌과 가야총림을 설립한 효봉 학눌이 ‘총림의 존재 이유’에대하여 어떻게 인식하고 있는가 하는 점이다.둘째는 만암이 고불총림을 설립하기까지 어떠한 수행을 하였으며 고불총림을 설립하기 위한 과정은 어떠했는가 하는 점이다. 이와 더불어 만암이설립한 고불총림의 성격과 그 활동이 어떠했는가 하는 점이다.셋째는 효봉이 가야총림을 설립하기까지 어떠한 수행과정을 겪었으며, 가야총림의 성격과 활동은 어떠했는가 하는 점이다.일제강점기를 지나 해방공간의 불교계는 혼란 속에서 다양한 모색을 시도하였는데 그것이 현대 한국불교의 성격을 결정지었다는 점에서 중요한의미를 지닌다. 고불총림과 가야총림은 선원 수좌들이 중심이 되어 종합적이고 모범적인 불교 도량을 건설하기 위한 움직임이었다. 그 역사적 의미가큼에도 불구하고 그동안 봉암사 결사에 비하여 불교계의 주목을 받지 못한측면이 있다. 본 논문은 해방공간 불교계의 활동에 대한 기존의 인식을 재고하고자 했다는 점에서 의의가 있다.

73권 호.title_kr: 서옹 석호와 토마스 베리의 문명론 비교 연구 - 현대문명 비판과 대안 문명론 -
73권 호.title_en: A Comparative Study of Seo-ong seokho and Thomas Berry’s Views on Civilization: Critique of Modern Civilization and Alternative Civilizational Discourse
73권 호.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 한국불교의 대표적 선지식 서옹(1912–2003)과 가톨릭 사제이자 생태철학자 토마스 베리(1914–2009)의 문명론을 비교하여 현대문명 비판과 대안 문명론에 대한 동서양 사상가의 차이와 공통점을 고찰한다. 두 사상가는 인류가 직면한 물질만능주의, 과학기술 중심주의, 생태계파괴, 인간성 상실 등의 위기를 심층적으로 성찰하며 종교적 지혜를 통해문명 전환의 길을 모색했다는 접점이 있다. 서옹은 선 수행과 ‘참사람’ 사상을 중심으로 물질문명 속에서 상실된 주체성을 회복하고 개인의 자각을 공동체적 실천으로 확장하는 ‘참사람 결사 운동’을 제창하였다. 베리는 테야르 드 샤르댕의 진화론적 우주관과 동양 철학에 기반하여, 근대 서구문명의 ‘진보의 신화’와 ‘인간중심주의’를 비판하고 ‘위대한 과업’으로서 생태대로의 이행을 주장하였다. 그러나 역사 이해에 있어서는 분명한 차이가 존재한다. 베리는 기독교 신학과 진화론적 우주론에 근거하여 역사를 목적론적ㆍ낙관적으로 해석한다. 이에 반해 서옹은 불교의 연기론에 입각해 절대적목적을 부여하지 않고 낙관주의를 경계하면서 ‘지금 여기’에서의 수행과 실천을 강조한다. 이러한 차이에도 불구하고, 두 사상가는 모두 욕망의 무제한적 팽창과 영성의 상실을 위기의 근원으로 진단한다. 그리고 인간 내면의 변화를 출발점으로 강조하고 존재를 상호의존적 관계망 속에서 이해하며 개인적 자각이 공동체적 실천으로 나아가야 한다는 점을 공유한다. 따라서 본 연구는 두 사상가의 비교를 통해 현대문명 위기 속에서 동서양 사상이 어떻게 교차하고 보완될 수 있는지를 밝히며, 종교적 성찰이 문명 전환 담론에 기여할 가능성을 모색한다.
73권 호.abstract_en: Seoong( 西翁, 1912–2003), a representative figure of modern Korean Buddhism, and Thomas Berry(1914–2009), a Catholic priest and ecological philosopher, in order to examine both the commonalities and differences between Eastern and Western thinkers in their critique of modern civilization and their visions of alternative civilization. Both thinkers shared a deep concern for the crises of materialism, technocentrism, ecological destruction, and the loss of human dignity, and sought pathways toward civilizational transformation through religious and philosophical wisdom. Seo-ong emphasized Zen practice and the idea of the “True Person” (Cham-saram), advocating the True Person Movement as a way to restore lost subjectivity within material civilization and to extend individual awakening into communal practice. Berry, drawing on Pierre Teilhard de Chardin’s evolutionary cosmology and Eastern thought, criticized the “myth of progress” and anthropocentrism in modern Western civilization, and proposed the advent of the “Ecozoic Era” as humanity’s “Great Work.” Despite these shared concerns, a significant difference arises in their historical perspectives.Berry, grounded in Christian theology and an evolutionary cosmology, interpreted history in a teleological and optimistic manner, presenting a vision of humanity’s progression toward a new civilization. In contrast, Seo-ong, rooted in the Buddhist principle of dependent origination (pratītyasamutpāda), refrained from assigning absolute purpose, remained cautious toward eschatological or overly optimistic perspectives, and emphasized practice and communal action in the “here and now.” Despite these differences, both thinkers converge in diagnosing the boundless expansion of desire and the loss of spirituality as the root causes of the crisis, and in underscoring inner transformation as the starting point for alternatives. They also share a relational worldview in which existence is understood as an interdependent web, and in which individual awakening must lead to communal practice. By comparing Seo-ong and Berry, this study highlights how Eastern and Western thought can intersect and complement each other in the face of civilizational crisis, and explores the potential contribution of religious reflection to discourses on civilizational transformation.

73권 호.title_kr: 해안 봉수의 무아사상에 대한 현대 심리학적 해석과 치유법 모색
73권 호.title_en: A Contemporary Psychological Interpretation of Haean Bongsu’s Thought of Non-Self and Its exploration of Therapeutic Practice
73권 호.abstract_kr: 본 연구는 해안(海眼, 1901~1974) 선사의 생애와 사상을 고찰하고󰡔해안집󰡕에 수록된 법어와 경전 해설을 중심으로 그의 무아사상을 분석하였다. 해안은 평생에 걸쳐 ‘7일 정진’을 강조하며 여러 경전에 대한 해설및 수행법을 제시하여 자아에 대한 집착의 해체와 무아적 통찰을 실생활속에서 구현할 것을 역설했다. 그러나 그의 사상과 수행관은 기존 학계에서 연구되지 못하고 있는 실정이다. 본 연구에서는 󰡔해안집󰡕에 수록된 법어와 경전 해설을 중심으로 해안 선사의 무아사상을 체계적으로 고찰하고이를 현대 심리학의 자아이론 및 마음챙김 기반 치유법과 비교하였다. 해안의 통찰은 현대 심리학의 탈중심화 이론, 자기심리학의 관계적 자아 개념, 그리고 마음챙김의 비판단적 수용 원리와 긴밀하게 연결된다고 본다.특히 그의 7일 정진 수행은 극한적 몰입과 단기간 돌파를 지향한다는 점에서 점진적 구조를 갖춘 MBSR이나 MBCT와 차별되지만 현대 명상 프로그램에 대한 심화과정이나 보완적 모델로서 의의가 있다.
73권 호.abstract_en: This study examines the life and thought of Ven. Haean (海眼, 1901–1974) and analyzes his doctrine of non-self (anattā) as articulated in the Haean-jip (海眼集), a collection of his Dharma talks and scriptural commentaries. Throughout his life, Haean consistently emphasized “seven-day intensive meditation” (chil-il jeongjin) and, through his interpretations of various scriptures and meditation methods, urged the dismantling of self-attachment and the realization of non-self in daily life.Nevertheless, his thought and practice have remained largely unexamined in existing scholarship. This study therefore systematically investigates Haean’s understanding of non-self based on the Haean-jip and compares it with contemporary psychological theories of the self and mindfulness-based therapeutic approaches. In his scriptural exegesis, Haean repeatedly stressed the importance of non-self, while his model of seven-day intensive practice highlighted the radical dismantling of self-attachment and the embodiment of insight in everyday conduct. Such perspectives resonate with modern psychology’s concept of decentering, the relational self in self-psychology, and the principle of non-judgmental acceptance central to mindfulness. In particular, Haean’s seven-day intensive meditation, which emphasizes extreme immersion and breakthrough within a short time span, stands in contrast to the gradual and structured formats of MBSR and MBCT, yet may serve as a deepening or complementary model for contemporary mindfulness programs.

73권 호.title_en: The Meaning of “Particle of Dust”(微塵) from a Contemplative Perspective in the Diamond Sūtra and the Lotus Sūtra
73권 호.abstract_kr: In the passages of the Diamond Sūtra and the Lotus Sūtra, a particle of dust — which reveals a wondrous world through the ceaseless repetition of birth and death across space-time — is mentioned. When the earth element of the trichiliocosm is perceived as dust, the particles drifting in the wind resemble the afflictions arising within the mind.In the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā, it is described that over countless eons, the rajās (dust particles) of the earth in the trichiliocosm are ground into powders to form a “paramāṇusaṃcaya” (collection of indivisible particles). Meanwhile, in the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka, it is envisioned that if one were to ascend like the paramāṇu (indivisible particles) through the infinite spatiotemporal realm and drop the paramāṇurajas (indivisible particles of dust) one by one, the world of emptiness — where everything returns to emptiness — would eventually unfold.If a practitioner were to alternately contemplate the passages in the Lotus Sūtra and the Diamond Sūtra that refer to a “particle of dust” and apply them to meditative practice, the in sight that the world of emptiness is precisely non-emptiness might momentarily arise at the end of contemplation.
73권 호.abstract_en: 시공간을 초월하여 끊임없이 생멸을 반복하면서 우리에게 놀라운 세계를보여주는 ‘미진(微塵)’은 실제 수행에서 관찰 대상이 되기도 하는데, 그러한 ‘미진’이 언급된 금강경과 법화경에서 삼천대천세계의 땅의 요소가흙먼지로 관찰될 때 바람에 흩날리는 먼지의 입자는, 마치 마음속 번뇌가요동치는 모습과 흡사해 보인다.Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā(금강경)에서는 무수한 겁을 지나는동안에 삼천대천세계에서 땅의 요소 중 rajas(미진)들을 가루로 부수어서‘paramāṇusaṃcaya(극미의 모음)’를 만든다고 가정하여 설하는 한편, Saddharmapuṇḍarīka(법화경)에서는 무한한 시공간의 세계에 있는paramāṇu(극미)들처럼 날아올라서 paramāṇurajas(극미진)를 하나씩하나씩 떨어뜨린다면, 언젠가는 그것이 다한 공(空)의 세계가 펼쳐질 것이라고 상상하여 설한다. 금강경은 티끌들의 가루로 빚은 극미의 모음이있는 불공(不空)의 세계를 암시하는데, 만약 수행자가 금강경과 법화경 에서 ‘미진’이 언급된 문장을 번갈아 보며 실제 수행에 접목해본다면, 그 문장의 끝부분에서 공즉불공(空即不空)의 세계가 찰나 보일지도 모른다.구마라집은 금강경과 법화경을 번역하면서 rajas, paramāṇu, paramāṇurajas를 모두 ‘微塵’이라 한역(漢譯)하여 독자들이 혼동하게 하나, 거듭 읽으면서 그 뜻을 되새기다 보면 ‘微塵’에 여러 의미가 함축되어있음을 알게 된다

73권 호.title_kr: 『법화경』과 남악 혜사·천태 지의의 법화삼매에 대한 사상적 연계 연구
73권 호.title_en: A Study on the Doctrinal Linkage of Dharma Flower Samādhi in the Lotus Sūtra, Nanyue Huisi, and Tiantai Zhiyi
73권 호.abstract_kr: This study aims to clarify, from a doctrinal–historical perspective, how the conception of the Lotus Samādhi presented in the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra (Lotus Sūtra) was concretized as a practical system of cultivation and systematized within Buddhist scholasticism through the interpretations of Nanyue Huisi(南嶽慧思) and Tiantai Zhiyi(天台智顗). While the Lotus Sūtra proclaims the Mahāyāna ideals of the One Vehicle(ekayāna) and the True Nature of All Dharmas(sarva-dharma-svabhāva / dharmāṇāṃ tattva), the text does not explicitly formulate a procedural method for the realization of samādhi. Accordingly, this study analyzes how the ideological elements concerning bodhisattva practice, peaceful practices(anle xing), and samādhi presented in the sūtra were reinterpreted by Huisi and Zhiyi, and further developed into concrete systems of cultivation.Huisi, in works such as the Fahua jing anle xing yi(法華經安樂 行義) and the Zhu fa wu zheng sanmei famen(諸法無諍三昧法門), established a dual structure of “form-based practice”(yǒuxiàng xíng) and “formless practice”(wúxiàng xíng), situating the Lotus Samādhi as an accessible and realistic praxis through the integration of peaceful practices, scriptural recitation, and contemplative insight. Zhiyi inherited these concerns and articulated a more comprehensive and coherent structure of cultivation, formulating doctrinal frameworks such as the Threefold Contemplation in One Mind(yīxīn sānguān) and the Four Samādhis (sizhong sanmei), thereby aligning the principle and practice of the Lotus Samādhi with the core of Tiantai scholasticism.This development process is not merely a linear succession of doctrinal interpretation but can be understood as an internal process of deepening—namely, the practical concretization of the sūtra’s archetypal ideal in Huìsī, followed by its scholastic systematization into an integrated and perfect(圓頓) contemplative framework by Zhiyi.In conclusion, this study demonstrates that the interpretations of Huìsī and Zhiyi positioned the Lotus Samādhi as a crucial medium by which the Mahāyāna ideal of “unity between doctrine and contemplative praxis”(jiaoxing yiti) is realized. It further suggests that their integrated approach to doctrine and meditation provides a practical model for overcoming the contemporary challenge of the separation between Buddhist practice and everyday life.
73권 호.abstract_en: 본 연구는  『법화경』의 법화삼매 관련 서술이 남악 혜사와 천태 지의를거치면서 어떻게 수행론적으로 구체화되고 교학적으로 체계화되었는지를사상사적 관점에서 규명하는 데 목적이 있다.  『법화경』은 일불승과 제법실상이라는 대승적 이상을 제시하지만, 이를 실천적으로 구현하기 위한 삼매수행의 절차나 방법은 명시적으로 제시하지 않는다. 이에 본 연구는 경전이 제공한 보살행·안락행·삼매의 이념적 요소가 혜사와 지의에 의해 어떠한 방식으로 재해석되고 수행 체계로 전개되었는지를 분석하였다.남악 혜사는 『법화경안락행의』와 『제법무쟁삼매법문』등을 통해 유상행과 무상행이라는 이원 구조를 설정하고, 안락행·경전 수지·공관 수행을 결합함으로써 법화삼매를 현실적 수행으로 자리매김하였다. 천태 지의는 혜사의 문제의식을 계승하여 일심삼관·사종삼매와 같은 원돈적 지관 체계를정립함으로써, 법화삼매의 수행 원리를 교학적으로 정합화하였다. 이러한전개 과정은 단순한 사상적 계승을 넘어, 『법화경』의 원형적 사상을 기반으로 한 수행의 실천적 구체화(혜사)가 다시 교학적 통합 체계(지의)로 심화되는 내적 발전 과정으로 이해될 수 있다.결론적으로 본 연구는 혜사와 지의의 해석을 통해 법화삼매가 대승불교수행 전통에서 ‘교리와 관행의 통합’을 구현하는 중요한 매개 역할을 했음을 밝혔다. 아울러 이들의 통합적 수행론은 현대 수행에서 제기되는 ‘수행과 일상의 분리’ 문제를 극복할 수 있는 하나의 실천적 모델을 제공함을 제시한다.

73권 호.title_kr: 『유가사지론약찬(瑜伽師地論略纂)』에 나타난 규기(窺基)의 유식비량(唯識比量)
73권 호.title_en: Kuiji’s Vijñaptimātratā Inference in Condensed commentary on Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra
73권 호.abstract_kr: 본 논문은 규기(窺基)의 󰡔약찬󰡕｢섭결택분｣의 주석에서 제시된 유식비량(唯識比量)의 의의를 고찰한 것이다. 규기는 아뢰야식의 존재를 성립시키는 여덟 가지 논제를 분석하면서 진나의 삼지작법(三支作法)을 적극 활용하였다. 특히 다섯 번째 논제를 다루면서, ‘일체유식(一切唯識)’을 성립시키는 자신의 유식비량을 제시하였다. 다섯 번째 논제란, ‘여러 식구들의 구전(俱轉)을 인정하지 않으면, 외적 기세계와 자기 신체와 아(我), 그리고 색(色) 등의 경계를 요별하는 네 가지 작용은 성립할 수 없다’는 것이다. 규기는 소승의 반론을 추정해서 반박 논증을 만들고, 이를 통해 ‘여러 식이동시에 일어나야만 네 가지 차별적 작용이 성립한다’는 것을 보여준다.나아가 그는 그 반박 논증들이 결국은 ‘일체유식’을 성립시키는 자신의유식비량으로 귀결된다는 것을 보여준다. 8식설에 따르면, 아뢰야식은 종자로부터 기세계와 신체를 변현해내어 그것을 인식하고, 말나식은 아뢰야식의 견분(見分)에 의지해서 ‘아’의 영상을 변현해내어 그것을 인식하며, 육식은 아뢰야식의 상분(相分)에 의지해서 각자의 경계를 변현해내어 그것을 인식한다. 이런 의미에서 일체법은 식과 분리되지 않는다. 아뢰야식과말나식을 전제해야 세계와 신체와 아를 요별하는 작용도 성립한다는 것은규기의 반박 논증들에 의해 뒷받침된다. 다만, 소승은 색 등의 경계를 육식이 요별한다는 것을 인정해도 그 경계가 식과 분리되지 않는다는 것을 인정하지 않는다. 여기서 규기는 그것을 성립시킨 논증으로 현장의 유식비량을 인용하였다.
73권 호.abstract_en: This paper examines the significance of Vijñaptimātratā inference (唯識比量) as presented in Kuiji’s commentary on the “Section on Determinations” (攝決擇分) of Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra.Kuiji actively employed Dignāga’s three-part syllogism analyzing eight theses that establish the existence of the ālaya-vijñāna. In particular, while addressing the fifth thesis, he introduced his own Vijñaptimātratā inference to affirm the doctrine of “everything is consciousness”.The fifth thesis asserts that unless the simultaneous arising of multiple types of consciousness is accepted, four distinct cognitive functions—discriminating the external natural world, one’s own body, the self, and objects such as form (rūpa)—cannot be established. This argument indirectly affirms the existence of the ālaya-vijñāna by logically responding to counterarguments from other Buddhist schools. Kuiji further constructs a rebuttal by anticipating objections from the Hīnayāna perspective, thereby demonstrating that only the simultaneous emergence of multiple consciousnesses can account for the four differentiated cognitive functions.Furthermore, Kuiji demonstrates that his rebuttal arguments ultimately converge on his own Vijñaptimātratā inference, which establishes the doctrine of “everything is consciousness”.According to the theory of the eight consciousnesses, the ālaya-vijñāna, relying on karmic seeds, manifests and cognizes the external natural world and one’s physical body. The manas-vijñāna, depending on the subjective aspect (darśanabhāga) of the ālaya-vijñāna, manifests and cognizes the image of the self. The six consciousnesses, relying on the objective aspect (nimitta-bhāga) of the ālaya-vijñāna, manifest and cognize their respective objects.In this framework, all phenomena (dharmas) are inseparable from consciousness. The necessity of positing both ālaya-vijñāna and manas-vijñāna to account for the discrimination of the external world, the body, and the self is substantiated by Kuiji’s rebuttal arguments. However, the Hīnayāna tradition, while acknowledging that the six consciousnesses discriminate objects such as material dharmas, does not accept that these objects are inseparable from consciousness.To address this, Kuiji cites Xuanzang’s Vijñaptimātratā inference as a logical proof to establish the inseparability of object and consciousness.
keywords_en: Condensed Commentary on the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra (瑜伽師地論略纂)
Vijñaptimātratā in terms of principle (理唯識)

73권 호.title_en: A Consideration of śūnyatā in Mūlamadhyamakakārikā - Focusing on the 7th verse of the 24th chapter -
73권 호.abstract_kr: This thesis examines emptiness (śūnyatā) in the Mūlamadhya makakārikā (MMK). Specifically, it refers not only to Candrakīr ti’s commentary Prasannapadā (PP) but also to other verses of the 24th chapter and to various chapters of the MMK, in order to clarify “the purpose of emptiness (śūnyatā prayojana)”, “empti ness (śūnyatā)”, and “the meaning of emptiness (śūnyatārtha)” m entioned in the 7th verse of that chapter.Emptiness, as can be seen from MMK 24:1-7 and MMK 13:1-4, is neither being (bhāva), which possesses the inherent nature of existence, nor non-being (abhāva), which possesses the inherent nature of non-existence; it is the non-inherent nature (niḥsvabhāvatv a), the characteristic that makes transformation possible.The meaning of emptiness, as can be seen from MMK 24:18, becomes clearly manifest within the equivalence relation “depen dent co-arising (pratītyasamutpāda) = emptiness = temporary designation (prajñapti) = the middle way (madhyamā pratipa d),” which is established on the basis of “non-inherent nature,” that is, “not arising while possessing inherent nature.” At this point, the meaning of emptiness is identical with the meaning of dependent co-arising (the mutual dependence of causes and conditions and the arising of things as their result), temporary designation (the designation of emptiness that depends on its o wn constituents), and the middle way (emptiness in which there is neither the inherent nature of existence nor the inherent nat ure of non-existence).Finally, the purpose of emptiness, as can be seen from MMK 18:1-5, can be understood in relation to the twelve links (dvādaśāṅga pratītyasamutpāda). In connection with both the structure of the state conditioned by deluded mind (pravṛtti mārga) and the state conditioned by true mind (nivṛtti mārga) of the twelve links, the purpose of emptines is the “cessation of conceptual proliferations (prapañca),” the “extinction of discriminations (vikalpa),” the “ext inction of karma (karman) and afflictions (kleśa),” and “liberation (mokṣa),” namely the “accomplishment of the state conditioned by true mind of the twelve links.” As discussed above, when the purpose of emptiness, emptiness, and the meaning of emptiness are interpreted not only in connec tion with the commentary but also organically with various chap ters of the MMK, their significance becomes all the more clear.
73권 호.abstract_en: 본 논문은 『중론송』의 공성에 관해 고찰한다. 구체적으로 말하자면, ｢관사제품｣ 제7송에 언급된 ‘공성의 목적’, ‘공성’, ‘공성의 의미’를 자세히 밝히기 위해 월칭의 주석서인 󰡔쁘라산나빠다󰡕는 물론이고, ｢관사제품｣의 다른게송들과 󰡔중론송󰡕의 여러 품까지도 참고한다.공성은 ｢관사제품｣ 제1-7송과 ｢관행품｣ 제1-4송을 통해 알 수 있듯이, 존재성이라는 자성을 지닌 존재도 아니고 비존재성이라는 자성을 지닌 비존재도 아닌 것이며, 변화를 가능하게 하는 특성인 무자성이다.공성의 의미는 ｢관사제품｣ 제18송을 통해 알 수 있듯이, ‘무자성’, 즉 ‘자성을 지닌 채로 발생하지 않는 것’을 매개로 하여 성립하는 ‘연기 = 공성= 가시설 = 중도’의 등가적 관계 가운데 분명히 드러난다. 이때 공성의의미는 연기(인과 연의 상호의존성과 그 과로서 사물이 발생하는 것), 가시설(공성의 가시설이 자신의 부분을 의존하는 것), 중도(공성 가운데 존재성이라는 자성도 없고 비존재성이라는 자성도 없는 것)의 의미와 같다.마지막으로 공성의 목적은 ｢관법품｣ 제1-5송 통해 알 수 있듯이, 십이연기와 관련하여 이해할 수 있다. 십이연기의 유전문과 환멸문과 관련하여알 수 있는 공성의 목적은 ‘희론의 멸진’, ‘분별의 소멸’, ‘업과 번뇌의 소멸’, ‘해탈’, 즉 ‘환멸문의 성취’이다.이상과 같이 공성의 목적, 공성, 공성의 의미는 주석서뿐만 아니라,『중론송』의 여러 품과 유기적으로 연결하여 해석할 때, 그 뜻이 더욱더 분명히 드러난다

73권 호.title_kr: 불교와 유목민 문화에 관한 고찰 –대비심의 관점에서-
73권 호.title_en: Buddhism and Nomadic Culture: In the Perspective of Compassion (snying rje)
73권 호.abstract_kr: 유목민족(遊牧民族)은 동북아시아와 중앙아시아 역사를 통틀어 대승불교의 발전과 확산 과정에 많은 영향을 주었다. 고대 서북인도부터 중세 아시아 각지에 이르기까지, 유목민족은 재가신자와 승려, 후원자 등의 역할을 적극적으로 수행했을 뿐 아니라 불법의 전파에도 직간접적으로 관여되어 왔다. 중관으로 대표되는 대승(보살승)과 밀승(금강승)의 두 측면을 모두 가진 티베트 불교는 유목민족과 불교의 관계를 잘 드러내는 대표적 사례이다. 본 연구에서는 유목민족들의 사고관이 대승불교, 나아가 티베트불교와 가지는 접점에 주목하여, 각각 환경적 측면과 사회적 측면, 그리고문화적 측면에서 분석해본다. 그리고 이를 바탕으로 일부 유목민족들이 불교를 적극적으로 수용한 직간접적 사유와, 그들이 불교에 어떤 영향을 끼쳤을지에 대해 고찰해본다. 지리적으로, 유목민족들은 일찍이 원거리 무역이 발달했는데, 이는 외부 신앙과 사상 유입을 용이하게 한다. 사회적으로는 행정인력과 식자층의 수요를 승려들이 해소하면서 지도층과의 상호의존관계가 형성되었다. 문화적으로는 사냥, 도축, 전쟁 등 죽음이 일상적인 반면, 가축을 정성껏 돌보고 가족애를 중시하는 대조적 측면이 함께 존재한다. 이는 죽음 너머의 가치, 그리고 자비와 중생의 구제를 설하는 대승불교및 금강승 불교 수용에 영향을 주었을 수 있으며, 나아가 티베트 불교에서자비심의 강조와 폭력적 이미지의 등장이 함께 나타나는 배경일 수 있다.유목민적 불교의 현존 사례인 티베트 불교에서 드러나는 방편 및 지혜의불이(不二)적 시각과 대비심(大悲心)의 강조는 북인도 밀교의 기반에 유목민적 사유관이 습합되어 발전한 영향일 수 있다.
73권 호.abstract_en: Nomadic peoples played a pivotal role in the development and dissemination of Mahāyāna Buddhism across Northeast and Central Asia. From Northwestern India to North and East Asia, nomads have actively served various roles as lay followers, monks, and patrons, partaking in the transmission of Buddhist teachings. Tibetan Buddhism, which encompasses both Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna traditions, represents the link between nomadic societies and Buddhism. This study focuses on the intersections of nomadic thought in relation to Mahāyāna and Tibetan Vajrayāna, studying it in environmental, social, and cultural perspectives, discussing the backdrops affecting the nomadic acceptance of Buddhism, and the potential nomadic influence on Buddhism. Geographically, long-distance trade routes of Nomads have facilitated the introduction of foreign religions and ideas. Socially, Buddhist monks undertook the role of administrative manpower, fostering reciprocal relationships with nomadic rulers. Culturally, the coexistence of contrasting ideas, such as common death in hunting, slaughter, and warfare, and care for livestock and familial bonds may have have become a factor in the reception of Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna; possibly pursuit of values beyond death, of compassion, and salvation of sentient beings, potentially contributing to the concurrent display of compassionate ideals and violent imagery in Tibetan Buddhism. The emphasis on non-dual perspective and the use of skillful means, and great compassion (snying rje chen po) prevalent in Tibetan Buddhism may thus be the influence of nomadic thoughts amalgamated with, and on the foundations of, North Indian Tantric Buddhism.
